message.content:
Work in /opt/nxeon. You are writing the definitive internal product manual for **Nxeon**, a Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform (Next.js App Router + Prisma/Postgres + a systemd job worker + Proxmox). It is about to go customer-ready, and the owner wants documentation substantially deepened: more sections, screen layouts, and end-to-end workflows.

YOU OWN: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` (the main deliverable). You may also create new files under `docs/` EXCEPT the three listed as forbidden below.

RENDERING TARGET — this is important, read carefully:
- The file is rendered at `/admin/docs` by `app/admin/docs/page.tsx` using an in-house renderer, `lib/markdown.ts`. Read BOTH before writing.
- The viewer **splits the document into sections at every `##` (H2) heading** and builds a searchable section list. So H2s are the navigation. Choose them deliberately: each H2 should be a topic someone would search for.
- Supported: headings, **bold**, *italic*, `inline code`, fenced code blocks, unordered/ordered lists, blockquotes, links, horizontal rules, and **GitHub-style tables** (table support was just added — use tables freely).
- NOT supported: mermaid, images, HTML, nested lists (a nested list renders flat — restructure instead).
- Therefore: draw all diagrams, screen layouts and workflows as **ASCII/box-drawing art inside fenced code blocks**. These render in a monospace `<pre>` with horizontal scroll, so they look good. Keep them under ~100 columns.

WHAT TO PRODUCE:

**1. Preserve the existing dated change-log sections.** The file already contains a long history of dated entries. Do NOT delete them. Restructure the document so reference material comes first and the historical log lives in a clearly-marked later part.

**2. Add a proper front section**: what Nxeon is, the architecture (web app / worker / Proxmox / Postgres / mail / nginx), the request and job lifecycles, and the environments (production `/opt/nxeon`, staging `/opt/nxeon-staging`). Include an ASCII architecture diagram.

**3. Per-feature chapters.** For EVERY significant feature, document: what it does, the customer-facing screen (ASCII wireframe), the step-by-step workflow (ASCII flow), the code entry points (`file:line` for the action/worker handler), the data model touched, failure modes, and how an admin diagnoses it. Cover at minimum:
server deployment & the deploy wizard; plans/pricing/terms; the wallet, checkout and wallet/card split; invoices; renewals, grace and suspension; server lifecycle ops (start/stop/reboot/reinstall/rename); resize up and down; per-server disk expansion; block-storage volumes and the portable-volume model; backups (scheduling, progress, retention); snapshots/restore; **server migration** (the flagship — give it the deepest chapter); the cPanel-style control panel (websites/PHP, databases, one-click apps, cron); the web console (noVNC); SFTP/file manager; domains (registration, DNS, transfer-in); Cloudflare OAuth integration; SSL/certificate issuance; Nxeon Mail (mailboxes, webmail, composer, signatures, settings); business email subscriptions; game servers and per-game config; Build with AI / Claude Code; teams & membership; support tickets and live chat; notifications; API tokens; 2FA/security; referrals, coupons, affiliate and gift codes; bandwidth metering; the admin portal surfaces; RBAC areas.

**4. Admin runbooks** — a section of concrete operational procedures: deploying a change, restarting services safely (NEVER restart the worker while a job is RUNNING — explain how to check the queue first), reading worker logs, diagnosing a stuck job, re-running a failed migration, issuing a certificate by hand, checking mail deliverability, and rolling back.

**5. Troubleshooting** — symptom → cause → fix tables, drawn from real incidents. `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md` contains a catalogue of real, confirmed migration failures; mine it heavily (do not edit that file).

**6. Data model reference** — walk `prisma/schema.prisma` and document each significant model, its important fields, and its relationships.

METHOD
- Investigate before writing. Read the actual code and cite real symbols and paths; every `file:line` you cite must be real. Do not invent behaviour — if you are unsure how something works, read it, and if it remains unclear, write what you verified and flag the gap explicitly rather than guessing.
- Where you find something documented that is no longer true, correct it and note the correction.
- Be genuinely useful, not padded. Someone should be able to operate and debug this platform from this document alone.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT edit `docs/AUDIT-24H.md`, `docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md`, or `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md` — other processes own those.
- Do NOT edit any source file. Documentation only. (You may READ anything.)
- Do NOT run `npm run build` or `npm run dev`, and do NOT restart any systemd service — production is live.
- Do NOT git commit or push.
- Never take a destructive or state-changing action on the live system or database. Read-only DB inspection is fine.

Report back: the new top-level structure (H2 list), roughly how much you added, and anything you found documented-but-wrong or that you could not verify.

Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

I'm noticing a potential bug with the inline code placeholder restoration—the regex pattern that matches space-digit-space could accidentally replace standalone numbers in regular text like "step 3 of 5" with undefined values if the corresponding code array entry doesn't exist. I need to be careful not to trigger this by avoiding that specific pattern in my output. So I need to be careful about how numbers appear in text — wrapping them in backticks makes them safe since the placeholder itself becomes a space-digit-space pattern that restores correctly. Numbers adjacent to units without spaces (like "4h") are also safe since the regex requires spaces on both sides. Numbers at sentence ends with periods or followed by commas are protected too. This applies everywhere inline rendering happens: tables, lists, headings. The global replace flag means overlapping patterns get consumed sequentially, which could create unexpected gaps in certain edge cases.

content.content:
1	# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform
2	
3	Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
8	- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
9	- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
10	- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
11	- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
12	- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).
13	
14	## Portals & design system
15	
16	- Customer portal (`app/dashboard/**`) and admin ops portal (`app/admin/**`) are separate sidebar apps sharing `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (sidebar, topbar, notifications bell, ⌘K command palette backed by `/api/search`).
17	- Design system lives in `app/globals.css` (glass cards, gradient buttons, navy palette) + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` + `components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free SVG charts). Use these — do not add chart libraries.
18	- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
19	- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners).
20	
21	## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)
22	
23	- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id).
24	- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
25	- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.
26	
27	## Conventions
28	
29	- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
30	- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
31	- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
32	- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
33	- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
34	
35	## Documentation — keep it current (required)
36	
37	- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
38	- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
39	- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
40	- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.
41	
42	## Commands
43	
44	- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
45	- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker`
46	- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
47	- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
48	- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
49	
50	## Domains & TLS
51	
52	- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
53	- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
54	- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP.
55	- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.
56	
57	## Environments
58	
59	- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
60	- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080. Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
61	- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
62	- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at :8080 → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. The improvement agent should test changes on staging before promoting.
63	
64	## Safety rules
65	
66	- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
67	- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
68	- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
69	- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
70	- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
71	- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.
72

1	# Nxeon — Complete System Documentation
2	
3	Exhaustive reference for the Nxeon VPS hosting platform: scope, architecture, every file, every
4	feature, every fix, and how it all works, in enough depth that a new engineer (or an AI reviewing
5	the system) can understand any part without reading the source. This is a **living document** — it
6	is updated in the same commit as every change, fix, or addition. Last updated 2026-07-23.
7	
8	- **Customer portal:** https://revsports.ca  ·  **Admin:** https://4j3d7gkr2wcbi34.revsports.ca  ·  **Staging:** https://staging.revsports.ca
9	- **Repo:** github.com/santino1233/nxeon (auto-push every commit)  ·  **Admin login:** `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
10	- **This page, hosted:** https://revsports.ca/docs (regenerated from this file by `scripts/publish-docs.mjs`)
11	
12	> **Reading guide.** Sections 1–5 are the big picture (what it is, how it's shaped, where it runs).
13	> Sections 6–8 are the internals (data, files, mechanisms). Sections 9–12 are the operational
14	> surface (features, fixes, integrations, day-to-day commands). Sections 13–15 are posture,
15	> backlog, and history. Every technical term is defined the first time it appears.
16	
17	## Table of contents
18	1. Scope & product
19	2. Architecture & request flow
20	3. Infrastructure (server, storage, network)
21	4. Environments & deploy pipeline
22	5. Domains, TLS & routing
23	6. Data model (every table)
24	7. Codebase map (every file)
25	8. Subsystems — how each works
26	9. Feature catalog
27	10. Fixes & hardening applied
28	11. Integrations & environment variables
29	12. Operations & scripts
30	13. Security model
31	14. Known gaps & roadmap
32	15. Change history
33	
34	---
35	
36	## 1. Scope & product
37	
38	Nxeon is a **self-serve cloud hosting platform** in the style of Hostinger and DigitalOcean. A
39	visitor signs up, adds funds, and in a few clicks has a running virtual server — with an operating
40	system, a control panel, an application, or a game server already installed — reachable over the
41	public internet. Everything is automated: there is no human in the provisioning loop. It runs on a
42	**single OVH dedicated server** in the **Singapore (sgp1)** datacenter, virtualized with **Proxmox
43	VE 9**, and is architected so that adding more servers ("nodes") scales capacity without any code
44	change.
45	
46	**What it sells**
47	
48	- **VPS (Virtual Private Server)** — a KVM virtual machine cloned from a cloud-init template. There
49	  are four plans (**Starter / Standard / Pro / Max**) that scale CPU cores, RAM, disk, and monthly
50	  bandwidth; the exact specs and prices are data rows editable at `/admin/plans`. Each plan can be
51	  ordered on one of two **storage tiers** — **NVMe** (fast, redundant mirror) or **HDD** (cheaper,
52	  bulk) — and on one of four **billing terms**: monthly, annual, 2-year, or 3-year, where longer
53	  commitments carry a discount (see §8, Billing).
54	- **One-click images** — beyond a bare OS, the deploy catalog offers ready-to-run software:
55	  **10 OS versions**, **7 control panels** (cPanel-style management UIs), and **19 applications**.
56	  The applications include **game servers** (Minecraft, Valheim, Rust, Palworld, CS2, Terraria),
57	  **VPNs** (WireGuard, OpenVPN), and **Caddy** for automatic HTTPS. Picking one runs its install
58	  script automatically on first boot via cloud-init.
59	- **Domains** — customers can search, register, renew, and manage DNS for domain names through the
60	  **name.com** registrar API, priced at a configurable **markup** over Nxeon's wholesale cost.
61	- **Dedicated IPv4** — an optional paid add-on that gives a VM its own public IPv4 address (rather
62	  than sharing one behind NAT), backed by **OVH failover IPs**.
63	- **Planned: "Build with Claude AI"** — a feature (already advertised on the marketing site and in
64	  the dashboard, backend pending) that connects Claude to a customer's server so they can build and
65	  configure it with plain-English prompts instead of a shell.
66	
67	**Who it's for, and the two portals.** The same codebase serves two very different audiences
68	through two separate sidebar applications:
69	
70	- The **customer portal** (`/dashboard`) is deliberately simple: deploy a server, manage it, pay,
71	  register domains, open a ticket.
72	- The **admin ops portal** (`/admin`) is a full operations center for running the business —
73	  customer management, the server fleet, the provisioning queue, finance, and infrastructure — with
74	  **role-based access control** so support and billing staff see only their areas.
75	
76	A **public marketing site** (landing page, pricing, features, legal pages) fronts both and converts
77	visitors into signups.
78	
79	---
80	
81	## 2. Architecture & request flow
82	
83	Nxeon is a **Next.js application backed by PostgreSQL**, paired with a **background worker** that is
84	the only component allowed to change a virtual machine. This split — web app decides *what* should
85	happen, worker makes it happen — is the single most important design decision in the system.
86	
87	| Layer | Technology | Role |
88	|---|---|---|
89	| Web | Next.js 15 (App Router, Server Actions), React 19, Tailwind v4 | Both portals + marketing + API, one process on port 3000 |
90	| Database | PostgreSQL 17 + Prisma ORM | Source of truth for all state |
91	| Worker | Node/`tsx` daemon polling a `Job` table → Proxmox API | Executes every VM mutation, owns the firewall |
92	| Hypervisor | Proxmox VE 9 (KVM) | Runs the customer VMs |
93	| Proxy / TLS | nginx + Let's Encrypt | Terminates HTTPS, routes by hostname, rate-limits auth |
94	| Payments | Stripe (live on prod, test on staging) | Funds customer wallets via Checkout |
95	| Domains | name.com v4 API (production on prod, dev-sandbox on staging) | Domain search/register/renew/DNS |
96	| Dedicated IPs | OVH API (failover IP + Virtual MAC) | Allocates/releases public IPv4 for VMs |
97	| Console | noVNC via a credential-safe websocket relay | In-browser VM console without exposing Proxmox creds |
98	
99	**How a request flows.** A browser hits nginx on 443. nginx terminates TLS, decides which portal
100	this hostname is (customer apex, secret admin subdomain, or staging host), applies the auth
101	rate-limit on login/register routes, adds security headers, and proxies to Next.js on `127.0.0.1:3000`.
102	Next.js renders the page or runs a **Server Action** (a function that executes on the server when a
103	form is submitted). Reads and writes go to Postgres via Prisma; read-only status/metrics calls may
104	go straight to the Proxmox API.
105	
106	**The golden rule — all VM mutations go through the `Job` queue.** When a customer clicks "reboot"
107	or "deploy," the web app does *not* call Proxmox to do it. It writes a row into the `Job` table
108	describing the desired change and returns immediately. The worker, polling that table every ~3
109	seconds, picks up the job and performs the actual Proxmox operation. This decoupling is what makes
110	provisioning **resilient** (a crash mid-operation is retried, not lost), **node-agnostic** (the
111	worker figures out which physical server the VM lives on), and **safe** (the public-facing web
112	process never holds destructive Proxmox power directly).
113	
114	---
115	
116	## 3. Infrastructure
117	
118	**The server.** One OVH **KS-GAME** dedicated machine: Intel **i7-7700K** (4 cores / 8 threads),
119	**64 GB RAM**, in datacenter **sgp1 (Singapore)**, public IP **51.79.162.96**. This single box runs
120	Proxmox, both the production and staging stacks, PostgreSQL, nginx, the worker, and every customer
121	VM. Capacity is finite and tracked (see §8, Multi-node) so the platform can scale to additional
122	nodes before this one fills.
123	
124	**Storage — three ZFS pools, chosen per workload.** ZFS is the filesystem/volume manager; each
125	"pool" is a set of disks presented as one storage target.
126	
127	- **`vmdata`** — a **mirror across 2×450 GB NVMe** SSDs (~344 GB usable, redundant against a single
128	  disk failure). This is the **premium tier**: fast and fault-tolerant. VM templates are cloned here
129	  by default.
130	- **`vmdata-hdd`** — a single **4 TB HDD** (~3.6 TB usable). This is the **bulk tier**: much more
131	  space, cheaper, slower, not mirrored. Plans on the HDD storage tier land here.
132	- **`backup`** — `/tank/backup` on the 4 TB pool — holds database and VM backups, the cloud-init
133	  snippet files the worker writes per server, and OS install ISOs.
134	
135	**Network — two bridges for two connectivity models.** A "bridge" is a virtual switch VMs attach to.
136	
137	- **`vmbr0`** — the **public bridge**, carrying the host's public IP with gateway `.254`.
138	  **Dedicated-IP VMs** attach here and get a real public IPv4 directly.
139	- **`vmbr1`** — a **private NAT bridge** on `10.20.0.0/24` with gateway `.1`. **Shared-IP VMs**
140	  (the default) attach here with a private address and reach the internet through NAT; inbound SSH
141	  (and any ports the customer opens) arrive via port-forwarding (DNAT) from the host's public IP.
142	
143	**Templates (VMID 9000–9009).** Ten cloud-init base images are pre-built and marked as Proxmox
144	templates: **Ubuntu 24.04 / 22.04 / 20.04**, **Debian 13 / 12 / 11**, **AlmaLinux 9 / 8**, and
145	**Rocky 9 / 8**. Provisioning clones one of these (a fast copy-on-write clone onto `vmdata`) rather
146	than installing an OS from scratch, which is why a server is ready in seconds. **VMIDs 9000–9999 are
147	reserved for templates and must never be touched except to add new ones.**
148	
149	---
150	
151	## 4. Environments & deploy pipeline
152	
153	There are two complete, isolated copies of the platform on the one server — **production** (what
154	customers use) and **staging** (a mirror for testing). They never share a database, a port, or a
155	pool of VM IPs, so nothing done in staging can affect a real customer.
156	
157	| | Production | Staging |
158	|---|---|---|
159	| Path | `/opt/nxeon` | `/opt/nxeon-staging` |
160	| Database | `nxeon` | `nxeon_staging` |
161	| Web / worker services | `nxeon-web` (:3000), `nxeon-worker` | `nxeon-staging-web` (:3001), `nxeon-staging-worker` |
162	| nginx ports | :80 / :443 | :8080 / :8443 |
163	| VM IP range / SSH port range | 10.20.0.**100–250** / **20000–29999** | 10.20.0.**50–99** / **30000–30999** |
164	| NAT firewall chain | `NXEON_FWD` | `NXEON_FWD_STG` |
165	| Stripe | **live** (`sk_live…`) | **test** (`sk_test…`) |
166	| name.com | production API | dev sandbox |
167	| Console relay port | :8899 | :8898 |
168	
169	**One codebase, `.env`-driven differences.** The two instances run *identical* code. Everything that
170	differs is an environment variable read from that instance's `.env`: `NXEON_ENV`, `NXEON_COOKIE_NAME`
171	(so sessions don't collide), `NXEON_NAT_CHAIN`, `NXEON_TAG` (Proxmox VM tag), `NXEON_IP_START/END`,
172	`NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END`, `PORT`, `APP_URL`, plus the credential sets. Because `.env` is
173	per-instance and **gitignored**, a deploy only ever copies code — the live-vs-test payment and
174	registrar split is permanent and can't leak across.
175	
176	**The deploy pipeline (also used by the nightly agent).**
177	
178	1. **Commit** locally. A `.git/hooks/post-commit` hook **auto-pushes to GitHub** over the deploy key.
179	2. **`scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]`** checks out the ref into staging, runs `npm run build`,
180	   applies any Prisma migrations, restarts the staging services, and **health-checks** `:8080`.
181	3. **Verify** on staging (`https://staging.revsports.ca`).
182	4. **`scripts/promote-production.sh`** rebuilds and restarts production once staging looks good.
183	
184	This staging-first flow is a hard rule for the autonomous improvement agent: it must prove a change
185	on staging before promoting it to production.
186	
187	---
188	
189	## 5. Domains, TLS & routing
190	
191	The platform's own domain is a **placeholder** (`revsports.ca`) until the real business domain is
192	purchased, and the entire system is built so that swapping it is a one-line change.
193	
194	**Single source of truth.** The domain is defined in exactly **one file**, `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`,
195	with four values: `BASE_DOMAIN`, `ADMIN_HOST` (the secret admin subdomain), `STAGING_HOST`, and
196	`CERTBOT_EMAIL`. **Nothing in the application code hardcodes the domain** — the app reads `APP_URL`
197	and `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated, never hand-written.
198	
199	**`scripts/configure-domains.sh`** is the generator. Running it: (1) writes the nginx vhosts for all
200	hosts; (2) obtains Let's Encrypt certificates over the webroot ACME challenge; (3) adds the auth
201	rate-limit `location` blocks, the `wss://…/console-ws` websocket proxy for the browser console, and
202	the public `/docs` location; (4) sets `APP_URL` and turns on `COOKIE_SECURE`; (5) reloads nginx.
203	
204	**Routing rules.**
205	
206	- **Customer portal** on the apex (`https://BASE_DOMAIN`) — requests to `/admin` here return **404**,
207	  so the admin panel's very existence is hidden from the public domain.
208	- **Admin ops portal** on the **secret subdomain** (`https://ADMIN_HOST`) — a random, unguessable
209	  hostname; its root redirects to `/admin`.
210	- **Staging** on its own host. All HTTP is 301-redirected to HTTPS. Certificates auto-renew via the
211	  certbot systemd timer.
212	- **`/docs`** on the apex serves this documentation as a static, `noindex` page (public, no auth —
213	  intended to be removed from public view before launch).
214	
215	**Migrating to the real domain** is therefore: edit `domains.env`, point the new domain's DNS
216	(A records for apex, `www`, the admin host, and the staging host) at `51.79.162.96`, and re-run
217	`configure-domains.sh`. That is the whole migration — see `docs/MIGRATION.md` for the runbook.

222	
223	All state lives in PostgreSQL, modeled with Prisma. After any schema edit, run `npm run db:push`;
224	seed the deploy catalog (panels/apps/games) with `npx tsx prisma/catalog.ts`.
225	
226	**Enums (the fixed vocabularies).**
227	- `Role` — `CUSTOMER / SUPPORT / BILLING / ADMIN` (drives RBAC).
228	- `ServerStatus` — `PENDING / PROVISIONING / RUNNING / STOPPED / SUSPENDED / REINSTALLING /
229	  DELETING / ERROR` (the VM lifecycle).
230	- `JobStatus` — queued/running/done/failed states for the worker queue.
231	- `JobType` — every operation the worker can perform: `PROVISION / START / STOP / REBOOT / REINSTALL
232	  / DELETE / SUSPEND / UNSUSPEND / RESIZE / SNAPSHOT_* / BACKUP_CREATE / SYNC_FORWARDS /
233	  PASSWORD_RESET`.
234	- `TicketStatus / TicketPriority`, `DomainStatus`, `ImageCategory` (`PLAIN_OS / CONTROL_PANEL /
235	  APPLICATION`), `DedicatedIpStatus` (`FREE / ASSIGNED / PENDING / RELEASING`), `NodeStatus`,
236	  `InvoiceStatus`.

239	- **User** — identity and wallet: `email`, `passwordHash`, `name`, `role`, `balanceCents` (the
240	  prepaid balance, in integer cents), `suspended`. Relates to servers, wallet transactions,
241	  projects, SSH keys, tickets, notifications, domains, invoices, and audit logs.
242	- **Plan** — a purchasable tier: `cpuCores`, `ramMB`, `diskGB`, `bandwidthTB`, `priceCents`,
243	  `storageTier` (nvme/hdd), `active`, `sortOrder`. Editable in the admin, so pricing/specs are data.
244	- **OsTemplate** — one entry in the deploy catalog: `slug`, `name`, `category`, `family`, `version`,
245	  `logo`, `vmid`/`baseVmid` (the template to clone), `setupScript` (installed on first boot),
246	  `minRamMB`/`minDiskGB` (requirements enforced at order time), `licenseRequired`, `featured`,
247	  `active`.
248	- **Server** — a provisioned VM: `hostname`, `vmid`, `status`, `ipAddress`, `sshPort`,
249	  `rootPassword`, `isFree` (comped servers skip billing), `autoRenew`, `termMonths`, `addons` (JSON),
250	  `wantsDedicatedIp`, `nodeId` (which physical node), bandwidth counters, `expiresAt`. Relates to
251	  its plan, OS template, node, jobs, port forwards, and dedicated IP.
252	- **Node** — a physical Proxmox host in the fleet: its own `apiUrl`/`tokenId`/`tokenSecret`/`pveNode`,
253	  `bridge`, `subnetPrefix`, IP and port ranges, `natChain`, `storages`, `capacityRamMB`, `isPrimary`,
254	  `enabled`, `status`. This is what makes the platform multi-node.
255	- **DedicatedIp** — one public IPv4 from the OVH pool: `address`, `ovhBlock`, `virtualMac`, `status`,
256	  `serverId` (when assigned), `reverse` (reverse-DNS/PTR).
257	- **Domain** — a customer's registered domain: `name`, `status`, `registrar`, `priceCents` (retail
258	  per year — what the customer pays), `costCents` (wholesale per year — what Nxeon pays name.com),
259	  `termYears`, `autoRenew`, `registeredAt`, `expiresAt`. Keeping retail and cost separate is what
260	  makes domain margin measurable.
261	- **Job** — a queued VM operation: `type`, `status`, `payload` (JSON), `error`, `attempts` (for the
262	  retry cap), `serverId`.
263	- **PortForward** — a customer-opened inbound rule: `publicPort`, `guestPort`, `protocol`.
264	- **WalletTransaction** — an immutable ledger line: `userId`, `amountCents` (negative = a charge,
265	  positive = a top-up), `description`.
266	- **Invoice** — `number` (autoincrement), `amountCents`, `taxCents`, `status`, `lineItems` (JSON),
267	  `period`, `paidAt`; rendered to printable HTML/PDF.
268	- **Ticket / TicketMessage** (support threads), **Project** (a customer's grouping/notes),
269	  **SshKey**, **Notification** (the in-app bell), **AuditLog** (who did what), **PasswordResetToken**
270	  (hashed, expiring, single-use), **Setting** (a key/value store for runtime config like SMTP).

377	## 8. Subsystems — how each works
378	
379	**Provisioning (deploying a server).** `orderServer` runs on the server when the deploy wizard is
380	submitted. It validates the chosen plan, image, term, and add-ons against capacity and the image's
381	requirements (e.g. minimum RAM), then **atomically debits the wallet** for the first term (plus the
382	dedicated-IP surcharge if selected) and, in the same transaction, creates the `Server` row and a
383	`PROVISION` job. The worker picks up the job and: resolves the server's node via `pveFor`, **clones**
384	the base template onto the correct storage tier, writes a **per-server cloud-init snippet** (SSH
385	keys, the generated root password, the image's `setupScript`, and any add-on installs), resizes the
386	disk to the plan size, configures networking (NAT on `vmbr1` **or** a dedicated IP on `vmbr0` via an
387	OVH Virtual MAC), starts the VM, and notifies the owner. If a step fails the job is **retried up to
388	3 times**; a **reaper** on worker startup re-queues any job left "running" by a crash so no server
389	gets permanently stuck.
390	
391	**Networking.** The default is **shared NAT**: the VM gets a private `10.20.0.x` address, and its SSH
392	port is DNAT-forwarded to a public port in the `20000–29999` range through the `NXEON_FWD` iptables
393	chain, which `worker/network.ts` rebuilds from the database. Customers can open additional TCP/UDP
394	forwards. The alternative is a **dedicated public IPv4** (OVH failover IP + Virtual MAC on `vmbr0`,
395	no NAT) for customers who need their own address. Free IPv6 for all servers is planned.
396	
397	**Billing.** Money is tracked as a **prepaid wallet** in integer cents; every charge is an atomic
398	conditional debit (`wallet.ts`) so races can't overdraw it. Customers add funds through **Stripe
399	Checkout**; the wallet is credited on the success-redirect confirm route, idempotently keyed by the
400	Stripe session so a double-load can't double-credit. **Commitment discounts** (`billing-terms.ts`):
401	VPS is **−10%** annual, **−15%** for 2 years, **−20%** for 3 years; domains get **−5% / −10%** for
402	multi-year. A **renewal sweep** runs every ~10 minutes: it auto-renews due servers from the wallet,
403	sends a warning before a server is at risk, grants a **3-day grace** period on failure, then
404	**suspends**, and finally **terminates** after the termination window — reclaiming the disk and any
405	dedicated IP. It also auto-renews domains. Every charge produces an invoice (printable / PDF).
406	
407	**Domains.** Backed by name.com v4. `checkDomains` returns both the **retail** price (Nxeon's
408	wholesale **cost** plus `DOMAIN_MARKUP_PCT`, default **25%**) and the cost. The customer is charged
409	retail; name.com is paid cost; the difference is Nxeon's margin, and both numbers are stored on the
410	`Domain` row so margin is auditable. The flow includes a **register wizard**
411	(domain → term → contact details → review), renewal, a DNS record manager, point-at-server, and
412	auto-renew.
413	
414	**Dedicated IPv4.** `dedicated-ip.ts` **syncs** OVH failover IPs into a local pool (the worker
415	refreshes it every ~5 minutes). On a dedicated-IP order it **claims** a `FREE` IP, **creates the OVH
416	Virtual MAC** (an asynchronous OVH task, so the code polls until it appears), and attaches the VM to
417	`vmbr0` with that MAC and `ip=<IP>/32,gw=51.79.162.254`. Deleting the server **releases** the IP and
418	Virtual MAC back to the pool. The admin IP-pool page shows cost, revenue, and margin per IP. This
419	path is **verified end-to-end on real OVH IPs**.
420	
421	**Multi-node.** Each `Node` row carries its own Proxmox credentials and IP/port pools. A scheduler
422	picks the **least-loaded enabled node** for a new server, and every worker handler is node-aware, so
423	the platform can span several physical hosts. `onboard-node.sh` prepares a fresh Proxmox host to join.
424	(Private networking *between* nodes would need a VPN/overlay — documented, not yet built.)
425	
426	**Console (in-browser VM screen).** `/api/console/[serverId]` mints a **JWE** (an encrypted token,
427	single-use, 60-second lifetime) containing the Proxmox VNC target. The browser connects to
428	`wss://…/console-ws`, which nginx proxies to `console-proxy.mjs`; that relay validates the token and
429	pipes the stream to Proxmox's `vncwebsocket`. **The Proxmox ticket never reaches the browser.** The
430	noVNC client itself is vendored in `public/novnc`.
431	
432	**Web terminal (in-portal shell).** From the Claude Code hub a customer clicks **"Open terminal &
433	start building"**, picks one of their running servers, and gets a real **xterm.js** root shell in a
434	slide-in panel — where they can run `claude` immediately. `POST /api/terminal/token` checks the
435	session (`requireUser`) and **ownership + RUNNING**, then mints a **JWE** (encrypted, 60-second)
436	token encoding only `{userId, serverId}` — the key is derived from `AUTH_SECRET` with a
437	terminal-specific salt (`lib/terminal-token.ts`), distinct from the console key. The browser opens
438	`wss://…/terminal-ws?token=…`, which nginx proxies to a standalone **`terminal-server/index.ts`**
439	(run by `tsx`, listening on `127.0.0.1:8901`, **not** bundled by Next). That backend **re-verifies**
440	the token and **re-checks ownership + RUNNING against the DB**, resolves host/port via
441	`connectionTarget`, decrypts the root password via `serverRootPassword`, opens an **ssh2 PTY shell**,
442	and pipes bytes both ways. **The root password never crosses the websocket and is never logged.**
443	Limits: **15 s** auth/connect, **10 min** idle, **60 min** hard cap; resize is handled. In
444	**SANDBOX** mode no SSH is opened — a simulated echo shell is piped so staging works. Deploy artifacts
445	live in `deploy/nxeon-terminal.service` (systemd) and `deploy/nxeon-terminal.nginx.txt` (nginx
446	location).
447	
448	**RBAC (staff roles).** `rbac.ts` maps **areas to roles**: `SUPPORT` sees overview/clients/support;
449	`BILLING` sees billing/invoices/subscriptions/plans; `ADMIN` sees everything. `requireArea` guards
450	each admin page, and the admin layout admits any staff role while filtering the nav per role.
451	`/admin/staff` lets ADMINs assign roles.
452	
453	**Email.** `mailer.ts` sends over SMTP (configured in admin Settings) with a local-Postfix fallback,
454	using branded templates — welcome, server-provisioned, payment receipt, renewal, suspension, and
455	password reset — wired into signup, payments, and the reset flow. `/admin/email-templates` shows a
456	**live iframe preview** of each template. (Real SMTP credentials are still required to actually send.)
457	
458	**Monitoring & backups.** A **nightly database backup** and a **weekly VM backup** write to
459	`/tank/backup`, each with an `OnFailure` admin alert; journald is size-capped. The **improvement
460	agent** works the top roadmap item every 4 hours through the staging→promote pipeline.

485	## 10. Fixes & hardening applied
486	
487	From the deep audit (2026-07-23) and throughout the build:
488	
489	- **Free-money `topUp` disabled when Stripe is live** — previously the demo top-up could mint wallet
490	  balance with no payment.
491	- **Firewall drops customer-VM→host traffic** — previously a tenant VM could reach the admin app,
492	  the Proxmox API, and host SSH.
493	- **Atomic wallet debits** across order/renew/domain — previously a concurrency race could drive a
494	  balance negative.
495	- **Stuck-job reaper on worker start** — previously a worker crash mid-job left a server permanently
496	  stuck.
497	- **Node-aware handlers** — previously deleting a VM on a second node orphaned it.
498	- **Domain multi-year sends the true registrar price** (previously rejected by name.com), and a
499	  **markup** was added (domains had been sold at cost, zero margin).
500	- **Resize proration** — previously mid-term upgrades were effectively free. **Cloud-init snippet
501	  cleanup** on server delete.
502	- **Dunning / termination** reclaims disk and IP from abandoned unpaid servers.
503	- **Build fixes** — `POPULAR_TLDS` and `GAME_FAMILIES` moved out of client / `"use server"` modules
504	  that may only export async functions.
505	- **Registrar and payments consolidated** — Namecheap removed in favor of **name.com** (prod +
506	  sandbox); **Stripe live/test split**. Plus nftables firewall, fail2ban, nginx auth rate-limit,
507	  HSTS and security headers, Let's Encrypt TLS with secure cookies, and the secret admin subdomain.
508	- **Marketing accuracy** — removed false claims ("dedicated IP on every plan," "isolated
509	  networking") and placeholder copy; replaced sketch/emoji icons with real brand logos.

561	## 13. Security model
562	
563	Defense in depth, from the network inward:
564	
565	- **Network.** An nftables `inet` firewall allows only SSH, HTTP/HTTPS, the staging ports, and
566	  Proxmox in, and **drops customer-VM→host traffic**; `fail2ban` bans brute-forcers; nginx applies an
567	  auth rate-limit on login/register plus HSTS, `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, a
568	  `Referrer-Policy`, and `server_tokens off`.
569	- **Transport.** Real Let's Encrypt TLS, `Secure` session cookies, and the admin panel on a
570	  404-hidden secret subdomain so it isn't discoverable from the public domain.
571	- **Application.** Every Server Action enforces `requireUser` / `requireStaff` / `requireArea` and
572	  an ownership check before touching a resource; the audit found **no IDOR** (no way to act on
573	  another user's object by guessing an ID). Impersonation is admin-only and is blocked from admin
574	  routes while active.
575	- **Data.** Atomic wallet debits prevent overdraw; password-reset tokens are hashed, expiring, and
576	  single-use; all secrets live in `.env` (600, gitignored) and never reach the client.
577	
578	Open security items are tracked in §14 (notably: lock down the Proxmox web UI + SSH, run the web
579	process as non-root, rotate the shared live Stripe key, and encrypt secrets/root-passwords at rest).

705	### Production-readiness audit wave (2026-07-24, commit `6791bff`)

708	- **Cross-tenant metrics leak (`/api/metrics`)** — `vmRrd` was always querying the *primary*
709	  Proxmox node, so a customer could read another tenant's series for a same-numbered VM on a
710	  secondary node. `vmRrd` is now node-aware and the route passes the server's own node connection.
711	- **Job-claim race** — the worker now claims each job with an atomic compare-and-swap
712	  (`updateMany where status=QUEUED → RUNNING`), so two workers can never run the same job.
713	- **Resize charge without delivery** — on terminal `RESIZE` failure the worker now reverses the
714	  up-front wallet movement (refund a failed upgrade, claw back a failed-downgrade credit),
715	  idempotent via an audit marker.
716	- **Account-deletion VM orphan** — `deleteMyAccount` now refuses while any server is still
717	  `DELETING`, so the cascade can't remove an in-flight teardown job and strand a live, billable VM.
718	- **Volume data-loss guards** — reinstall refuses while any block-storage volume is pinned to the
719	  server (its disk lives under the vmid and would be purged); server-delete cleans up the dangling
720	  volume rows, stops their billing, and notifies the owner.
721	- **Unsuspend with an empty IP pool** — now falls back to shared NAT (reconfigures `net0` + assigns
722	  an SSH port) instead of booting with a stale public config pointing at a reassigned failover IP.
723	- **Game-server oversell** — `orderGameServer` now runs the same `capacityCheck` the VPS order does.
724	- **Settings actually enforced** — ~15 previously-inert knobs are wired: `max_servers_per_user`,

Carried on `Migration.items.totalBytes`. 1143 - **Compatibility**: source vs target OS/arch — arch mismatch (red), distro-family mismatch (amber) with a 1144 soft "reinstall to matching OS" recommendation (closest OS-template deep-link). No block except storage. 1145 - **Marketing**: `/migrate` landing page + homepage section with animated `MigrationScreens`. 1146 1147 ## Mail — signature image upload 1148 1149 `SignatureImage` model (bytes in Postgres); `POST /api/mail/signature-image` (auth, byte-validated via 1150 `validateImageBytes`, 5 MB, per-user cap 20) returns an absolute https URL; public `GET 1151 /api/mail/signature-image/[id]` serves it (unguessable cuid, image-only). The signature editor's image 1152 button uploads-from-PC first (URL fallback); the inserted https `` survives `safeHtml` and renders in 1153 recipients' inboxes. 1154 1155 ## Domain transfer-in (inbound transfers) 1156 1157 The revenue-generating counterpart to the pre-existing transfer-OUT (unlock + EPP). Customers bring a 1158 domain they own at another registrar INTO Nxeon. 1159 1160 - **Registrar wrappers** (`lib/registrar.ts`, name.com v4 `/v4/transfers`): `checkTransfer(domain)` 1161 (transferable? price?), `createTransfer(domain, authCode, purchaseCents)`, `getTransfer(domain)`, 1162 `cancelTransfer(domain)`, `listTransfers()`, plus `transferOutcome()` / `transferStatusLabel()` 1163 helpers and `transfersAvailable()`. Same Basic auth / dev-host / error handling as the rest of the 1164 client. Transfer pricing falls back through three sources (the domain's own availability result → 1165 `:getPricing` → a throwaway probe name on the same TLD) because transfers bill at the TLD's RENEWAL 1166 rate. In `NXEON_SANDBOX` every wrapper returns synthetic data (names containing `locked` are 1167 non-transferable, `fail` rejects at submit, and a transfer progresses pendingOwnerApproval → 1168 pendingRegistry → completed on a compressed few-minute clock) so staging works untouched by name.com. 1169 - **Schema** (additive): `DomainStatus` gains `TRANSFER_PENDING` / `TRANSFER_FAILED`; `Domain` gains 1170 `isTransferIn`, `transferAuthCodeEnc` (AES-256-GCM via `lib/crypto-box`, scrubbed on completion or 1171 failure, never logged), `transferStartedAt`, `transferStatus` (raw registrar status), `transferEmail`. 1172 - **Wizard** `/dashboard/domains/transfer` (`DomainTransferInWizard`): domain check → a four-item 1173 pre-flight gate the customer must tick and the server re-validates (unlocked at the current registrar; 1174 WHOIS privacy off / auth code obtainable; >60 days since registration or last transfer — ICANN, not 1175 policy; able to approve the confirmation email) → auth code → review + submit. 1176 - **Money** (`lib/actions-domains-transfer.ts`): server-side re-quote (the client's price is never 1177 trusted — a drift aborts with the new price), then `createTransfer` at the registrar FIRST and only 1178 then one `$transaction` doing debit + wallet transaction + PAID invoice + the `Domain` row. Charging 1179 for an unsubmitted transfer is therefore structurally impossible; double-charging is blocked by the 1180 in-process submit guard, the UNIQUE `Domain.name` (or a CAS off the retried row's status) inside the 1181 charging transaction, and name.com refusing a second in-flight transfer. If the debit fails after a 1182 successful submit we cancel at the registrar and audit-log `domain.transfer_in.uncharged`. 1183 - **Status poll** (`domainTransferInSweep` in `worker/billing.ts`, on the existing 10-minute billing 1184 cadence): completed → ACTIVE with dates from `domainInfo` and the auth code scrubbed; failed → 1185 `TRANSFER_FAILED` with the registrar's reason and the wallet credited back; still pending → refresh 1186 the raw status and nudge the customer (deduped, every 3 days) to approve the losing registrar's email. 1187 Settlement goes through the CAS-guarded helpers in `lib/domain-transfer.ts`, so a re-run, two workers, 1188 or a simultaneous customer cancel can never credit twice. 1189 - **Cancel**: `cancelTransferIn` credits the wallet ONLY after the registrar confirms the cancellation — 1190 never on an assumption — and says so plainly if the registrar refuses (usually because the transfer 1191 already completed). 1192 - **Copy** is honest throughout: 5–7 days, not instant; the approval email comes from the OLD registrar; 1193 the 60-day ICANN window; the transfer adds a year on top of the existing expiry. 1194 1195 ## Cloudflare integration — "Connect Cloudflare", then DNS sets itself up 1196 1197 Cloudflare was previously a hidden, email-only setting (paste an API token inside the Business Email 1198 DNS panel). It is now an **account-level integration** with a real OAuth flow, reused by every DNS 1199 surface. Nothing about the DNS record mechanics changed — `lib/cloudflare-dns.ts` still takes a bearer 1200 token per call — only how we obtain that token, and how many places can use it. 1201 1202 - **OAuth (preferred)** — `lib/cloudflare-oauth.ts`. Authorization Code + PKCE (S256) as a 1203 CONFIDENTIAL client (`client_secret_post`). Endpoints, confirmed from Cloudflare's docs and their live 1204 OIDC discovery document: authorize `https://dash.cloudflare.com/oauth2/auth`, token 1205 `https://dash.cloudflare.com/oauth2/token`, revoke `https://dash.cloudflare.com/oauth2/revoke`. 1206 Cloudflare supports ONLY authorization_code (plus refresh_token) for third-party clients. The exact 1207 resource scope names could not be confirmed from public docs (they mirror API-token permission names 1208 — "Zone Read" + "DNS Write" — and are enumerable only via an authenticated 1209 `GET /client/v4/oauth/scopes`), so the requested scopes live in one env-overridable constant: 1210 `CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_SCOPES`, defaulting to `zone:read dns_records:edit offline_access`. 1211 - **Routes** — `GET /api/integrations/cloudflare/start` (requireUser, rate-limited, mints CSRF `state` 1212 + PKCE verifier into a 10-minute httpOnly cookie along with the intent and return path, redirects to 1213 Cloudflare) and `GET /api/integrations/cloudflare/callback` (verifies `state` against the cookie, 1214 exchanges the code, stores credentials, runs the pending action, redirects back). 1215 - **Auto-add on connect** — the cookie carries a validated intent (`email` / `website` / `migration` / 1216 `settings`, `lib/cloudflare-connect-intent.ts`). Immediately after consent, `runConnectIntent` 1217 (`lib/cloudflare-intent-run.ts`) calls the SAME ownership-checked server action the button would have 1218 called, so "sign in with Cloudflare → records published" takes zero extra clicks. Result flags ride 1219 back as `?cf=`/`?cfdns=`/`?cfmsg=` and render through `CloudflareResultBanner`. 1220 - **No schema change** — `User.cloudflareTokenEnc` holds EITHER an encrypted JSON credential blob 1221 (`{accessToken, refreshToken, expiresAt, scope}`) or, for anyone who connected before OAuth, a bare 1222 API token. `readStoredCloudflare` sniffs the shape; `resolveCloudflareToken` refreshes an expiring 1223 access token, re-encrypts the blob and hands back a usable bearer token. A failed refresh surfaces a 1224 friendly "reconnect Cloudflare" message instead of throwing. Every Cloudflare call — mail records 1225 included — now goes through that accessor. 1226 - **Paste-a-token fallback** kept behind an "Advanced" disclosure, and used automatically when 1227 `CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` / `_SECRET` are unset (`cloudflareOauthConfigured()` hides the button), 1228 so nothing breaks before the OAuth client is registered. 1229 1230 ### DNS surfaces built on it 1231 1232 - **Websites tab** (`pointWebsiteDns` in `lib/actions-websites.ts`, UI in `cpanel/WebsitesPanel.tsx`) — 1233 a checkbox on the add-website form plus a per-row "Point DNS" button. Upserts an **A record** for the 1234 site's hostname → the server's dedicated IP (else `Server.ipAddress`). `listWebsites` now also returns 1235 `serverIp` + `cloudflareConnected` to drive the control. 1236 - **Post-migration cutover** (`getMigrationDnsInfo` / `pointMigrationDns` in `lib/actions-migrate.ts`, 1237 `PostMigrationDns` in `MigrationWizard.tsx`) — the last manual step of an otherwise one-click 1238 migration. Candidate domains come from the customer's `Domain` rows, websites already on the target 1239 server, and hostnames inferable from the STORED scan snapshot (`Migration.items.scan` web-root folder 1240 names — no new source-scanning), plus a free-text box. `?migration=` deep-links back into the 1241 completed-migration view after a consent round trip. 1242 - **Settings** (`CloudflareIntegration`, `lib/actions-cloudflare.ts`) — connected/not-connected state, 1243 Connect button, advanced token paste, and Disconnect (clears the blob; best-effort revoke at 1244 Cloudflare for OAuth connections). 1245 1246 **A records are always written `proxied: false` (DNS-only).** That is load-bearing, not a default: the 1247 name must resolve to the customer's own server so Let's Encrypt's HTTP-01 challenge reaches certbot on 1248 that box — behind Cloudflare's proxy the challenge is answered at their edge and one-click SSL fails. 1249 An existing A record at the same name is UPDATED, never duplicated, so a repoint can't round-robin 1250 between the old and new server. Copy is honest everywhere: DNS changes take a few minutes to propagate. 1251 1252 In `NXEON_SANDBOX` nothing touches Cloudflare: `/start` stores a synthetic credential blob and runs the 1253 intent inline, and every record write returns a clearly-labelled synthetic success. 1254 1255 **Env vars** (`/opt/nxeon/.env`): `CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, and 1256 optionally `CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_SCOPES`. Register the redirect URL `/api/integrations/cloudflare/callback` 1257 on the Cloudflare OAuth client (Manage Account → OAuth clients), grant type `authorization_code`, 1258 response type `code`, token auth method `client_secret_post`. 1259 1260 --- 1261 1262 ## Per-server disk expansion — "my server just needs more disk" 1263 1264 Grows **one server's own root disk** without touching its plan's CPU/RAM/price. Distinct from 1265 block-storage volumes: a volume is portable and detachable, this space is fused into the VM's root 1266 filesystem. Sold at both the deploy step and on a running server. 1267 1268 **GROWTH IS ONE-WAY.** A live filesystem cannot be shrunk without risking data loss, so there is no 1269 shrink path anywhere and `Server.extraDiskGB` is never decremented. The permanence is stated on the 1270 Add-ons card, the Review step, the Add-storage card, the browser confirm dialog, the Stripe Checkout 1271 line, and every invoice line item. 1272 1273 ### Schema + pricing 1274 - `Server.extraDiskGB Int @default(0)` — GB purchased **beyond** `plan.diskGB`. A server's effective 1275 disk is always `plan.diskGB + extraDiskGB` (`effectiveDiskGB()`), and that is what every display, 1276 capacity sum and monitoring sample uses. 1277 - `JobType.DISK_EXPAND`. 1278 - Admin setting **`extra_disk_gb_price_cents`** (default `10` = $0.10/GB/mo, matching block storage), 1279 editable under Settings → Billing. 1280 - `lib/extra-disk.ts` — **pure, client-safe** constants + maths (`effectiveDiskGB`, `extraDiskCentsAt`, 1281 `normalizeExtraDiskGB`, `maxAddableExtraDiskGB`, `EXTRA_DISK_ONE_WAY_NOTE`). No server imports, so the 1282 wizard and the server action compute identical numbers — displayed === charged, like `wallet-split.ts`. 1283 - `lib/disk-expand.ts` — server-side core: `extraDiskPerGbCents()`, `extraDiskMonthlyCents(gb)`, 1284 `diskExpandQuote()`, `applyDiskExpand()`. Deliberately mirrors `lib/resize.ts` line-for-line. 1285 1286 ### Two purchase surfaces 1287 1. **Deploy upsell** (`DeployWizard` Add-ons step) — 0–500 GB slider in 10 GB steps, showing `+$X/mo` 1288 and the resulting total disk. Priced over the term exactly like the dedicated-IP add-on (no term 1289 discount, no promo) and folded into "Due today" and the wallet/card split. Flows through 1290 `orderSchema` → `orderQuote` → `placeOrder`, which persists `extraDiskGB` **before** the PROVISION 1291 job so the worker resizes `scsi0` straight to the full size — the VM is born the right size. 1292 2. **Post-deploy "Add storage"** (`components/customer/AddStorage.tsx`, top of the Resize tab) → 1293 `expandServerDisk()` in `lib/actions-disk.ts`: `requireUser` + ownership + impersonation guard + 1294 rate limit (5 / 10 min per user) + steady state (RUNNING/STOPPED) + no in-flight job. The charge is 1295 **prorated over the remaining term** with the same maths as `resizeQuote`. 1296 1297 ### Money path (why it can't double-charge) 1298 Identical contract to the plan resize: `walletSplit` applies the wallet first and the card is charged 1299 **only the remainder**. If the remainder is $0 the wallet is debited immediately inside the same 1300 `$transaction` that creates the job (rolled-back charge ⇒ no job). Otherwise the customer goes to 1301 Stripe (`createDiskExpandCheckout`); `/api/stripe/confirm` credits the card amount and then calls 1302 `applyDiskExpand` with the **full** proration, netting to zero — the wallet is never touched before the 1303 card clears, and `creditCheckoutSession`'s `UNIQUE(stripeSessionId)` makes a replayed confirm URL a 1304 no-op. A PAID invoice + wallet transaction are written with a dedicated extra-disk line item. 1305 1306 ### Worker `DISK_EXPAND` (`worker/disk-expand.ts`) 1307 Reads the live `scsi0` size → **skips Proxmox entirely if it is already at the target** → otherwise 1308 `PUT .../resize` with `size=+G` (Proxmox only grows) and waits for the task → then grows the 1309 guest **online** over SSH: detect root device + fs type with one read-only probe, validate every token 1310 against a shell-inert allowlist (`lib/ssh-exec.ts`, reject-never-sanitize), install `cloud-guest-utils` 1311 if needed, rescan the device, `growpart`, then `resize2fs` / `xfs_growfs` / `btrfs resize`. Progress is 1312 reported throughout via the standard job progress bar. `Server.extraDiskGB` is written **only after the 1313 disk really grew**. Every step is idempotent, so a retry is safe. 1314 1315 - **Never marks the server ERROR** — `DISK_EXPAND` is deliberately absent from `VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS`, 1316 since growing a disk doesn't change the VM's run state. 1317 - **Never leaves a customer paying for invisible space** — if the online grow can't happen (server 1318 stopped, unreachable, LVM/exotic layout, missing tools) the job still SUCCEEDS, because the disk *is* 1319 bigger; the notification names the reason and gives the **exact commands** to finish by hand. 1320 - **Refunds a genuine failure** — `reconcileFailedDiskExpand` credits the proration back (with a 1321 notification) but only when `extraDiskGB` never reached the job's target, so the partial-success path 1322 is never wrongly refunded. 1323 - SANDBOX simulates the whole sequence with real progress + a synthetic success. 1324 1325 ### Renewals + plan-resize interaction 1326 - `worker/billing.ts` and `renewNow()` both add `extraDiskGB × extra_disk_gb_price_cents × months` on 1327 top of the plan every cycle, as its own invoice line. The renewal-warning threshold includes it too. 1328 - **Plan resize preserves it.** `extraDiskGB` is additive to whichever plan the server is on, so the 1329 resize path never writes it, and the worker sizes the disk to `newPlan.diskGB + extraDiskGB` (using 1330 the bare plan size would ask Proxmox to *shrink* the disk of any server holding extra storage and the 1331 whole resize would hard-fail). It also **can't double-charge**: the proration is a difference of plan 1332 monthly prices and the extra-disk surcharge is identical on both sides, so it cancels exactly. 1333 - The disk-shrink guards in `resizeQuote` / `resizeServerDown` compare **plan** disks on purpose — 1334 since the extra is added to both sides, that is exactly the condition for "effective disk doesn't 1335 shrink". 1336 1337 ## Build with AI — one nav entry, API key moved into Settings (2026-07-25) 1338 1339 The customer sidebar carried **two** overlapping AI entries under Compute — "Build with AI" 1340 (`/dashboard/build`, the in-app plan-then-approve planner, which also hosted the BYOK key form) and 1341 "Claude Code" (`/dashboard/claude-code`, the pre-installed-CLI hub). Customers without a key saw the 1342 planner page as little more than an API-key input, so the two entries read as one broken feature. 1343 1344 - **Sidebar (`app/dashboard/layout.tsx`)** — now exactly one entry under Compute: 1345 `{ label: "Build with AI", href: "/dashboard/claude-code", icon: "rocket" }`. The old 1346 `Build with AI → /dashboard/build` (icon `bolt`) item is gone; the old `Claude Code` label is gone. 1347 The `feature_claude_builder` flag in `FEATURE_HREF` was re-pointed from `/dashboard/build` to 1348 `/dashboard/claude-code` so the admin toggle still hides the single entry. 1349 - **BYOK key lives in Settings** — `ClaudeKeyConnect` (unchanged component, unchanged 1350 `lib/actions-claude-key.ts` server actions: `connectAnthropicKey` / `disconnectAnthropicKey` / 1351 `hasAnthropicKey`, AES-256-GCM via `encryptSecret`) now renders on `/dashboard/settings` between the 1352 Cloudflare integration and Security cards, wrapped in `
`. Deep link: 1353 **`/dashboard/settings#anthropic-key`**. `connect`/`disconnect` revalidate `/dashboard/settings` as 1354 well as `/dashboard/build`. 1355 - **`/dashboard/build` kept, de-navved** — the planner still has real behaviour (ClaudeBuilder, 1356 recent-builds table, terminal button) and `worker/claude.ts` posts notifications whose `href` is 1357 `/dashboard/build`, so the route must keep resolving. Its key card was removed; its header is now 1358 "AI build planner" (was "Build with Claude AI") to stop colliding with the nav label, and the 1359 no-key amber card links to `/dashboard/settings#anthropic-key`. Reachable from notifications and 1360 the hub cross-link. 1361 - **Copy** — hub cross-link now says "AI build planner" and points at Settings for the key; 1362 `submitBuild`'s no-key error reads "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use Build with AI"; 1363 the `/dashboard/claude-code` `metadata.title` is now `"Build with AI"` (was `"Build with Claude 1364 Code · Nxeon"`, which also double-suffixed under the root title template). 1365 1366 ## Migration verification gate — a migration can no longer report success while a site is dark (2026-07-25) 1367 1368 A real customer migration finished, wrote `status: "DONE"`, and logged `Sites actually serving: 4/4` 1369 while **six** domains were unreachable. The customer opened studionexis.com and got a browser 1370 certificate warning, then Apache's default page. Everything below exists because of that run. 1371 1372 **Why the `4/4` was false — two independent bugs in one number:** 1373 - The **denominator was the domains we chose to publish**, not the domains the source actually 1374 served, so the metric was incapable of failing. 1375 - The probe only checked **HTTP status**, so `nexis.revsports.ca` counted as "serving" while 1376 returning the Apache2 Debian Default Page from `/var/www/html`. 1377 1378 **Root causes of the outage itself (all confirmed live on vmid 102):** 1379 1380 | Cause | Detail | 1381 | --- | --- | 1382 | `needrestart` wedged `apt` | `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive` does **not** suppress it on Ubuntu 22.04+. A certbot install blocked on `/usr/lib/needrestart/dpkg-status` for the full 10-minute `INSTALL_TIMEOUT_MS` — which *was* the HTTPS window. Two domains finished on plain HTTP. | 1383 | `/usr/local/bin/node` missing | `nexis-next.service` / `nexis-staging.service` had `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/node …`; target only had `/usr/bin/node` v20. `status=203/EXEC`, **78 crash-loops**, migration still reported success. | 1384 | `/opt/nexis` never built | No `.next/BUILD_ID`, so `next start` exits 1 in a loop even once node resolves. | 1385 | `apache2` re-enabled | Re-enabled from the source while we generated an nginx config; failed to bind and sat `enabled + failed` — a latent hazard on next reboot. | 1386 | studionexis.com had no vhost | Fell through to the `nexis.revsports.ca` default block → wrong cert (`ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID`) + Apache's leftover `index.html`. | 1387 1388 **What now prevents each (`worker/migrate-real.ts`, `worker/migrate.ts`):** 1389 - `APT_ENV` / `APT_OPTS` — `NEEDRESTART_MODE=a NEEDRESTART_SUSPEND=1`, a preceding 1390 `dpkg --configure -a`, and `--force-confdef/--force-confold`. 1391 - **Honest scoring** — `sourceDomains` captured from the source's own vhost config *before* any 1392 publish decision. Domains past the 24-name probe cap report as "not checked", never as serving. 1393 - **`defaultPageReason`** — Apache/nginx/RHEL welcome pages and near-empty 2xx bodies are **not 1394 serving**. `servedCertNames` + `certCoversName` read the cert actually presented via 1395 `openssl s_client -servername`; no CN/SAN coverage is **not serving**. 1396 - **`parseUnitExecPaths`** pre-flight — missing `ExecStart` binaries are symlinked from a 1397 `command -v` match or rsynced from source; if unresolvable **the unit is not enabled at all**, 1398 because enabling a known-broken unit only creates a reboot-persistent crash loop. 1399 - **Unit health gate** — `NRestarts` sampled twice 15s apart; crash-loopers carry their real journal 1400 tail and can never land in `verifiedRunning`. The Next.js "Could not find a production build" 1401 case is named explicitly with `next build` as the fix. 1402 - **`standDownOtherWebServers`** — stops, disables and **masks** the web servers we did not choose. 1403 - **`withHeartbeat`** — a line every ~45s on package installs, image transfers and cert issuance, so 1404 nothing sits silent at 89% again. 1405 1406 **Outcome plumbing (the part that makes it real).** `runRealMigration` returns 1407 `outcome: "COMPLETED" | "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES"` plus `outcomeReasons` / `unservedDomains` / 1408 `blockers`. `worker/migrate.ts` previously hardcoded `status: "DONE"` — with that line intact none of 1409 the above could ever reach the customer. It now writes `COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES`, and the notification 1410 **leads with the dark domains** and states the old server is untouched so DNS can be pointed back. 1411 `MigrationWizard` treats the new status as terminal (otherwise it polls forever and never renders), 1412 and `statusColors` gives it amber — with no entry it fell back to `STOPPED`'s neutral grey, which 1413 reads as "nothing to see", the exact false reassurance the status exists to prevent. 1414 1415 > **Process note.** `/usr/local/bin/node` was already written up as item 13 in 1416 > `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md` after an earlier incident, fix and all — and recurred verbatim. 1417 > A documented fix that nothing reads is not a fix. Incidents become executable checks now. 1418 1419 **Not yet true:** this gate has never run against a real migration. It is untested code on the most 1420 consequential path in the product. A scratch-VM rehearsal that asserts the gate is the outstanding 1421 work — until then the next real migration is its first test. 1422 1423 ## Storage pre-flight double-count — postmortem (2026-07-25, commit `05e6605`) 1424 1425 `lib/actions-migrate.ts` added the Docker image allowance into `items.totalBytes`, but 1426 `worker/migrate-real.ts` reads that value as `fileBytes` and adds the Docker allowance **itself**. A 1427 ~12 GB move was therefore reported as needing **83.6 GB** and refused. The contract is now stated at 1428 the return site: `items.totalBytes` is **files only** (selected paths + the DB data-dir estimate); 1429 the worker owns the Docker + headroom arithmetic. 1430 1431 **Customer impact:** the inflated figure led to a purchase of ~40 GB of disk that was not needed. 1432 Disk growth is deliberately one-way (no shrink path exists), so that spend is unrecoverable — 1433 recorded here because the money consequence, not the arithmetic, is why this must not recur. 1434 1435 ## Billing: subscription renewals have no card auto-charge (2026-07-25, finding) 1436 1437 Renewals debit the **wallet only**. `worker/billing.ts` charges via `debitWallet`; on 1438 `InsufficientBalanceError` it falls through to grace and then suspends. There is **no saved-card path 1439 anywhere**: no `setup_future_usage`, no SetupIntent, no `off_session` `PaymentIntent`. 1440 `User.stripePaymentMethodId` exists in the schema but is **never written and never read** (only a 1441 mention in `app/api/account/export/route.ts`). `User.autoRechargeEnabled` / 1442 `autoRechargeThresholdCents` / `autoRechargeAmountCents` are settable through 1443 `lib/actions-billing-prefs.ts` — whose own comment concedes "the actual off-session Stripe charge is 1444 wired by the orchestrator" — but **nothing calls that action and nothing consumes those columns**. 1445 1446 Consequence: a customer with a perfectly good card is suspended when their wallet empties. Agreed 1447 design — **wallet credit applied first, card auto-charged for the remainder** (consistent with 1448 `walletSplit`, which checkout already uses), dunning retries on days 1/3/5, suspension only after the 1449 card genuinely fails. Six dunning templates now exist on `emails.*` in `lib/mailer.ts` 1450 (`paymentReceipt`, `paymentFailed`, `paymentRetryFailed`, `paymentActionRequired`, 1451 `paymentFinalNotice`, `cardExpiringSoon`); the charging engine itself is **not built yet**. 1452 1453 --- 1454 1455 *Companion docs: `CLAUDE.md` (agent/ops conventions), `ROADMAP.md` (backlog), `docs/MIGRATION.md` 1456 (server migration).* 1457

content.content:
1	# Customer Migration — Field Notes & Failure Catalog
2	
3	Real-world failures observed running the lift-and-shift migration against a live
4	customer server, with the fix for each. **This is the acceptance criteria for the
5	migration engine**: a customer should be able to migrate, point DNS, and have their
6	site serve over HTTPS with no server access.
7	
8	Source of truth for these findings: a real migration on 2026-07-25 from a
9	HestiaCP/Hostinger box (Debian, nginx 1.25, 72.62.69.9) to a fresh Nxeon VPS
10	(Ubuntu 22.04, nginx 1.18, 1 vCPU / 2 GB / 25 GB).
11	
12	---
13	
14	## The architectural lesson
15	
16	**Do not blind-copy the source's `/etc/nginx` (or `/etc/apache2`) tree.** That single
17	behaviour caused roughly half of the failures below. Copying wholesale imports the
18	source's `nginx.conf`, its include layout, its panel-specific vhosts, its IP
19	bindings, and its certificate paths — none of which are valid on the target.
20	
21	Instead:
22	1. **Parse the source vhosts for intent** — server_name(s), document root or upstream
23	   proxy target, port, TLS on/off.
24	2. **Generate clean configs for the target's own web-server version.**
25	3. Leave the target's `nginx.conf` and include layout **intact**.
26	4. Copy the source config tree to a reference dir only
27	   (`/root/nxeon-migrations/<id>/source-nginx/`), never into live config.
28	
29	---
30	
31	## Failure catalog
32	
33	### Web server / routing
34	
35	| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix |
36	|---|---------|---------|-----|
37	| 1 | Source `nginx.conf` overwrote the target's | `include sites-enabled/*` disappeared → a generated vhost is **silently ignored** | Write vhosts where the *live* `nginx.conf` actually includes; verify with `nginx -T \| grep <server_name>`, not just `nginx -t` |
38	| 2 | Hardcoded source IP in ~21 configs | `bind() to <old-ip>:80 failed (99)` — nginx won't start | Rewrite source IP → target IP everywhere, or generate configs without IP binding |
39	| 3 | `/etc/letsencrypt` not migrated | 5 vhosts referenced missing certs + `options-ssl-nginx.conf` → config test fails → **web server down** | Migrate `/etc/letsencrypt` (certs, renewal conf, accounts) **or** strip TLS blocks and re-issue via certbot after DNS points over. Never leave a config referencing a missing cert |
40	| 4 | Web-server version mismatch | `http2 on;` (nginx ≥1.25) is an unknown directive on 1.18 | Detect target nginx version; translate/neutralise incompatible directives |

48	
49	| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix |
50	|---|---------|---------|-----|
51	| 10 | Docker **images** not migrated | Standalone containers using locally-built images (`app/frontend:latest`, never in a registry) can never start | `docker save \| gzip` on source → stream → `docker load` on target. Prefer `docker pull` for public-registry images |
52	| 11 | App configured for the **old domain** | `PUBLIC_APP_URL`/`PUBLIC_API_URL` pointed at the old host — and frameworks like Astro/Next **bake the API URL into the static bundle at build time**. Page loads; nothing works | Detect old-hostname references in copied env; offer to rewrite **and rebuild** the affected image. A frontend calling the old server's API is a *silent* failure |
53	| 12 | Secrets in a non-standard env file | compose had `${VAR}` placeholders but no `.env` — real file was `prod.env` (used via `--env-file`) | Detect the env file the project actually uses; if placeholders would resolve empty, **refuse to start** and name the missing vars |
54	| 13 | Absolute binary paths differ between hosts | Migrated systemd units called `/usr/local/bin/node` (manual install on source); target has `/usr/bin/node` (apt) → unit crash-looped **880 times** | Resolve `ExecStart` binaries; symlink or rewrite the unit to the target's real path |

62	|---|---------|---------|-----|

97

101	said `Sites actually serving: 4/4`.

103	Five separate failures, all now closed in `worker/migrate-real.ts`.
104	
105	| # | Failure | Symptom | Fix (implemented) |
106	|---|---------|---------|-------------------|
107	| 22 | **The success metric could not fail** | Log line 1: `Sites actually serving: 4/4`. The denominator was "domains we chose to publish", so it was 100% by construction | Denominator is now every hostname the **source** served, taken from its own live vhost config before we decide what we can publish (`sourceDomains`). The score is `served/total` against that set, the unserved ones are named, and a run with any unserved domain returns `outcome: "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES"` |
108	| 23 | **A 200 from the distribution's default page counted as "serving"** | The existing "make a real request to each domain" probe passed for a domain answering 200 with the Apache2 Debian Default Page | The probe now fetches the **body** as well as the status. Apache "It works!" / "Apache2 Debian Default Page" / "Apache2 Ubuntu Default Page" / "Apache HTTP Server Test Page", nginx "Welcome to nginx!", and empty/near-empty 2xx bodies are all **not serving**. Content is only judged on a 2xx (a 301→HTTPS or a 404 legitimately has a tiny body); short JSON/XML bodies are exempt so an API vhost is never called dark |

Missing ⇒ symlink to the same basename found via `command -v`, else copy the file from the source, else **do not enable it** and record a blocking entry naming the unit and the path |

112	| 27 | **Two web servers, one port 80** | `apache2` was re-enabled from the source's service list while we generated an nginx config. 113	| 28 | **Ten minutes of silence at 89%** | The progress bar sat frozen while `apt-get install certbot` ran. 116	
117	**This failure was already in this document.** It is item 13, written up after an
118	earlier migration where the same `/usr/local/bin/node` mismatch crash-looped a unit
119	880 times, with the fix spelled out: *"Resolve `ExecStart` binaries; symlink or
120	rewrite the unit to the target's real path."*
121	
122	It recurred anyway, on a different customer, four months later — because a documented
123	fix is not a fix. Nothing in the engine read this file. **That is why #25 is now an
124	executable pre-flight check that runs before every `systemctl enable`, not a
125	paragraph.** The general rule this establishes: a failure mode that has been observed
126	twice belongs in code, and a field note describing a fix nobody implemented is worth
127	approximately nothing.
128	
129	### Outcome semantics
130	
131	`runRealMigration` now returns `outcome: "COMPLETED" | "COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES"` plus
132	`outcomeReasons`, `sourceDomains`, `unservedDomains` and `blockers`. A migration is
133	`COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES` when any domain the source served does not serve here, when
134	any domain could not be checked, or when any migrated unit is not running.
135	
136	`Migration.status` in `prisma/schema.prisma` is a plain `String` (not a Prisma enum),
137	but the only writer is `worker/migrate.ts`, which sets `status: "DONE"`
138	unconditionally and persists **only** `summary.results` into `Migration.items.results`.
139	So the outcome is also emitted as the **first entry of `results`** — step
140	`Migration outcome: COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES`, status `failed` — which is what actually
141	reaches the customer's screen today. Wiring `summary.outcome` through to
142	`Migration.status` / a dedicated column is a one-line change in `worker/migrate.ts`
143	that has not been made.

5	/**
6	 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
7	 *
8	 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
9	 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
10	 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
11	 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with

14	export type Area =
15	  | "overview"
16	  | "analytics"
17	  | "clients"
18	  | "support"
19	  | "fleet"
20	  | "billing"
21	  | "platform";
22	
23	/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
24	export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
25	  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
26	  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
27	  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
28	  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
29	  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
30	  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
31	  platform: ["ADMIN"],

34	export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
35	  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
