input.content:
# Nxeon — Platform Manual

The operating manual for the Nxeon VPS hosting platform: what it is, how every feature works
end to end, how to run it, and how to debug it when it breaks. Written to be sufficient on its
own — someone with SSH to the box and this document should be able to operate and diagnose the
platform without reading the source.

Rendered privately for staff at `/admin/docs`. Source of truth: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.

## About this manual

**How it is organised.** The document is split into five parts. The viewer at `/admin/docs`
turns every `##` heading into a searchable section, so the headings below are the navigation —
search the section list rather than scrolling.

| Part | Sections | What it covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I — Platform | Architecture through Feature flags | What Nxeon is, how it is shaped, where it runs |
| II — Features | Deploy through RBAC | One chapter per feature: screen, workflow, code, failures |
| III — Operations | Runbooks and Troubleshooting | Concrete procedures and symptom-to-fix tables |
| IV — Reference | Data model, Job types, Settings | Tables, fields, enums, knobs |
| V — History | Every `Changelog ·` section | The dated build log, preserved unchanged |

**How each feature chapter is structured.** The same seven headings every time, so you can jump
straight to what you need:

- **What it does** — one paragraph, no marketing.
- **The screen** — an ASCII wireframe of what the customer actually sees.
- **The workflow** — the ordered steps from click to completion.
- **Code entry points** — real `file:line` references for the action and the worker handler.
- **Data model** — the tables and fields written.
- **Failure modes** — what actually goes wrong, and what the customer sees when it does.
- **How an admin diagnoses it** — which page, which log, which query.

**Conventions used throughout.**

- `file:line` references are real and were verified against the tree at the time of writing. If
  a line has moved, the symbol name next to it is still correct — search for that.
- "The worker" always means `worker/index.ts` running under `nxeon-worker.service`.
- "An action" means a Next.js Server Action — a function in a `"use server"` module that runs on
  the server when a form is submitted or a client component calls it.
- Money is always integer cents. Never introduce a float into a money path.
- **Anything marked GAP is a verified hole**, not a guess. Anything marked CORRECTION replaces
  something that earlier documentation stated and that is no longer true.

**A hard rule that explains most of the design.** Every mutation of a virtual machine goes
through a row in the `Job` table. The web process never calls a Proxmox mutation endpoint. Read
that sentence twice — it is the reason provisioning survives a crash, the reason the platform can
span nodes, and the reason a compromised web process cannot destroy the fleet.

---

## What Nxeon is

Nxeon is a self-serve cloud hosting platform in the style of Hostinger and DigitalOcean. A
visitor signs up, adds funds, and within a couple of minutes has a running virtual server —
with an operating system, a control panel, an application or a game server already installed —
reachable from the public internet. There is no human in the provisioning loop.

It runs on a single OVH dedicated server virtualised with Proxmox VE 9, and is architected so
that adding more physical hosts ("nodes") adds capacity with no code change.

**What it sells.**

- **VPS** — a KVM virtual machine cloned from a cloud-init template. Plans are database rows
  editable at `/admin/plans`, so specs and prices are data, not code. Four plans are active
  today (see Plans, terms, promos and pricing).
- **Deploy catalog images** — 36 templates are seeded, of which 10 are plain OS versions, 7 are
  control panels and 19 are applications, including six game families, VPNs and Caddy. Picking
  one runs its `setupScript` on first boot through cloud-init.
- **Game servers as their own product** — 14 `GamePlan` tiers priced per game and per size,
  distinct from the VPS plans they are provisioned on.
- **Domains** — search, register, renew, transfer in, transfer out and full DNS management via
  the name.com v4 API at a configurable markup over wholesale.
- **Business email** — 3 `EmailPlan` tiers selling mailboxes on a customer's own domain, backed
  by the self-hosted Mailcow instance.
- **Add-ons** — dedicated IPv4, block-storage volumes, permanent per-server disk expansion,
  scheduled backups.

**Two portals, one codebase.**

- The **customer portal** at `/dashboard` is deliberately simple: deploy, manage, pay, register
  domains, open a ticket.
- The **admin ops portal** at `/admin` is a full operations centre — customers, fleet, queue,
  finance, infrastructure — with role-based access control so support and billing staff see only
  their areas.
- A **public marketing site** fronts both.

**Current scale** (read from the production database at the time of writing): 6 users, 4
servers, 1 node, 34 jobs lifetime, 6 migrations. This is a pre-launch platform. Treat every
"verified in production" claim in this document as verified on a handful of real objects, not
at scale.

---

## Architecture

Five processes and one hypervisor. The web app decides what should happen; the worker makes it
happen. That split is the single most important design decision in the system.

```
                              INTERNET
                                 │
                                 │ :80 / :443            :8080 / :8443
                                 ▼
                    ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │  nginx  (TLS, vhost routing, rate limits,   │
                    │          security headers, ws upgrade)      │
                    └───┬──────────┬───────────┬──────────┬───────┘
                        │          │           │          │
           /  /dashboard│    /admin│  /console-ws   /terminal-ws
                        │          │           │          │
                        ▼          ▼           ▼          ▼
              ┌───────────────────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
              │  nxeon-web.service    │  │ console- │  │ nxeon-       │
              │  Next.js 15 :3000     │  │ proxy    │  │ terminal     │
              │  pages + actions +    │  │ .mjs     │  │ ssh2 PTY     │
              │  /api routes          │  │ :8899    │  │ :8901        │
              └───────┬───────────────┘  └────┬─────┘  └──────┬───────┘
                      │                       │               │
        writes Job rows│  reads state          │ VNC relay     │ SSH to guest
                      ▼                       │               │
              ┌───────────────────────┐       │               │
              │   PostgreSQL 17       │       │               │
              │   database `nxeon`    │       │               │
              │   (single source of   │       │               │
              │    truth for state)   │       │               │
              └───────┬───────────────┘       │               │
                      │ polls Job every 3s    │               │
                      ▼                       │               │
              ┌───────────────────────┐       │               │
              │ nxeon-worker.service  │       │               │
              │ worker/index.ts       │       │               │
              │ runs as root:         │       │               │
              │  · all VM mutations   │       │               │
              │  · iptables NAT chain │       │               │
              │  · billing sweeps     │       │               │
              └───────┬───────────────┘       │               │
                      │  Proxmox API (token)  │               │
                      ▼                       ▼               ▼
              ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
              │              Proxmox VE 9  (KVM hypervisor)            │
              │  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌───────────┐  │
              │  │ customer │ │ customer │ │ nxeon-   │ │ templates │  │
              │  │   VM     │ │   VM     │ │ mail VM  │ │ 9000-9009 │  │
              │  │ vmbr1 or │ │          │ │ Mailcow  │ │ (never    │  │
              │  │  vmbr0   │ │          │ │ vmid8000 │ │  touch)   │  │
              │  └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └───────────┘  │
              │  ZFS: vmdata (NVMe mirror) · vmdata-hdd · backup       │
              └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                       │
                        OVH API (failover IPs, virtual MAC, PTR)
                        Stripe API (checkout) · name.com API (domains)
                        Cloudflare API (DNS) · Anthropic API (BYOK)
```

**Component responsibilities.**

| Component | Unit | Port | Owns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Web app | `nxeon-web.service` | 3000 | Pages, server actions, `/api` routes, all reads |
| Worker | `nxeon-worker.service` | — | Every VM mutation, the iptables NAT chain, all sweeps |
| Console relay | `nxeon-console-proxy.service` | 8899 | noVNC websocket relay; holds the Proxmox ticket |
| Terminal backend | `nxeon-terminal.service` | 8901 | ssh2 PTY websocket; holds the guest root password |
| Database | PostgreSQL 17 | 5432 | All state |
| Hypervisor | Proxmox VE 9 | 8006 | Customer VMs |
| Reverse proxy | nginx | 80/443 | TLS, vhost routing, websocket upgrade |
| Firewall | `nxeon-firewall.service` | — | nftables host policy (oneshot) |
| Mail DNAT | `nxeon-mail-nat.service` | — | Mail-port DNAT to the Mailcow VM (oneshot, `RemainAfterExit=yes`) |

The staging stack mirrors this exactly with its own units (`nxeon-staging-web`,
`nxeon-staging-worker`, `nxeon-staging-console-proxy`, `nxeon-terminal-staging` on 8902).

**Why the worker runs as root.** It rebuilds the iptables DNAT chain from the database
(`worker/network.ts:28` `syncPortForwards`) and writes per-server cloud-init snippets to
`/tank/backup/snippets`. Neither is possible unprivileged. The web process does not need root
and does not have it.

---

## Request lifecycle

What happens between a customer clicking a button and something changing.

```
 Browser                nginx              Next.js (:3000)          Postgres        Worker
    │                     │                      │                     │              │
    │ 1. POST /dashboard  │                      │                     │              │
    │    (form submit)    │                      │                     │              │
    ├────────────────────▶│                      │                     │              │
    │                     │ 2. terminate TLS     │                     │              │
    │                     │    pick vhost        │                     │              │
    │                     │    auth rate-limit   │                     │              │
    │                     │    security headers  │                     │              │
    │                     ├─────────────────────▶│                     │              │
    │                     │                      │ 3. resolve session  │              │
    │                     │                      │    (JWT cookie,     │              │
    │                     │                      │     lib/auth.ts)    │              │
    │                     │                      ├────────────────────▶│              │
    │                     │                      │ 4. requireUser()    │              │
    │                     │                      │    ownership check  │              │
    │                     │                      │    rate limit       │              │
    │                     │                      │    in-flight-job    │              │
    │                     │                      │    guard            │              │
    │                     │                      │                     │              │
    │                     │                      │ 5. $transaction:    │              │
    │                     │                      │    debit wallet     │              │
    │                     │                      │    write row(s)     │              │
    │                     │                      │    INSERT Job       │              │
    │                     │                      ├────────────────────▶│              │
    │                     │                      │                     │              │
    │                     │◀─────────────────────┤ 6. revalidatePath   │              │
    │◀────────────────────┤    HTML / redirect   │    return           │              │
    │  "Queued…"          │                      │                     │              │
    │                     │                      │                     │◀─────────────┤
    │                     │                      │                     │ 7. poll 3s   │
    │                     │                      │                     │    CAS claim │
    │                     │                      │                     │──────────────▶
    │  8. page polls job progress / notification bell picks up the result             │
```

**Step 4 is where all security lives.** Every action re-derives the user from the session cookie
and re-checks ownership of the object by id. There is no trust in anything the client sent
except the id, and the id is always joined against `userId`. Prices are always re-quoted
server-side; a client-supplied price is never charged.

**Step 5 is where all correctness lives.** Money movement, the row it pays for, and the `Job`
that delivers it are written in one `$transaction`. A rolled-back charge therefore leaves no
job and no invoice. This pattern repeats in `lib/order.ts:195`, `lib/actions-disk.ts`,
`lib/resize.ts` and `lib/actions-domains-transfer.ts`.

**Reads do not go through the queue.** Status, metrics, file listings and service status are
read directly — from Postgres, from the Proxmox read-only API, or over SSH. Only mutations are
queued.

---

## Job lifecycle and the worker loop

The queue is a single Postgres table polled by one process. There is no broker, no Redis, no
cron. Everything the platform does asynchronously happens here.

```
                 ┌──────────┐
   action        │  QUEUED  │◀──────────────── retry (attempts < 3)
   INSERTs ─────▶│          │◀──────────────── reaper on worker start
                 └────┬─────┘
                      │  worker/index.ts:1136
                      │  UPDATE Job SET status='RUNNING', attempts=attempts+1
                      │  WHERE id=? AND status='QUEUED'      ← atomic claim (CAS)
                      │  count===1 ? I own it : someone else took it, re-poll
                      ▼
                 ┌──────────┐
                 │ RUNNING  │  handlers[job.type](job)      worker/index.ts:763
                 └────┬─────┘  progress/step written via reportJobProgress (:693)
                      │
            ┌─────────┴──────────┐
            │ resolves           │ throws
            ▼                    ▼
       ┌────────┐        attempts < 3 ? ──yes──▶ back to QUEUED (error recorded)
       │  DONE  │                 │
       └────────┘                 no
                                  ▼
                            ┌──────────┐
                            │  FAILED  │
                            └────┬─────┘
                                 │  worker/index.ts:964
                                 ├─▶ reconcileFailedJob()  — reverse the money
                                 │      RESIZE up   → refund the proration
                                 │      RESIZE down → claw back the credit
                                 │      DISK_EXPAND → refund unless it landed
                                 ├─▶ if type ∈ VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS → Server.status=ERROR
                                 └─▶ if type === PROVISION → release dedicated IP,
                                        clear Server.ipAddress (it is UNIQUE)
```

**The numbers that matter.**

| Constant | Value | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Poll interval | 3000 ms | `worker/index.ts:34` `POLL_MS` |
| Max attempts | 3 | `worker/index.ts:35` `MAX_ATTEMPTS` |
| Backup retention | keep latest 2 | `worker/index.ts:39` `CUSTOMER_BACKUP_KEEP` |
| Clone task timeout | 600 s | `worker/index.ts:271` |
| Backup task timeout | 3600 s | `worker/index.ts:747` |

**`VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS`** (`worker/index.ts:49`) is the whitelist of job types whose terminal
failure marks the server `ERROR`: `PROVISION`, `REINSTALL`, `DELETE`, `RESIZE`, `START`, `STOP`,
`REBOOT`, `SUSPEND`, `UNSUSPEND`, `BACKUP_RESTORE`, `SNAPSHOT_ROLLBACK`. Everything else — a
failed backup, a failed website creation, a failed SSL issue, a failed disk expansion — leaves
the server's status alone, because those operations never touch the VM's run state. `DISK_EXPAND`
is deliberately absent and this is load-bearing: growing a disk cannot break a running VM, and
flagging the server `ERROR` for it would be a lie.

**One in-flight job per server** is enforced at enqueue time, not in the worker. Every action
counts `Job` rows with status in `(QUEUED, RUNNING)` for that `serverId` and refuses (or silently
debounces) when the count is non-zero — see `lib/actions.ts:472`. This is why a wedged `RUNNING`
job blocks every subsequent operation on that server, and why the reaper exists.

**The reaper** (`worker/index.ts:1000` `reapStuckJobs`) runs once at worker start. Every job left
`RUNNING` by a crash or a restart is re-queued if it has attempts left, or failed with
`"Worker restarted mid-job"` if it does not — and in the failed case a server sitting in
`PROVISIONING`, `REINSTALLING` or `DELETING` is moved to `ERROR` so it is visibly broken rather
than invisibly stuck.

**Sweeps run on the same loop**, gated by elapsed-time checks, so they never overlap a job:

| Sweep | Cadence | Function | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Billing (renew, grace, suspend, terminate, domains, transfers) | 10 min | `billingSweep` | `worker/billing.ts:42` |
| Add-on product renewals (email, volumes) | 10 min | `productRenewalSweep` | `worker/product-renewals.ts:520` |
| Monitoring alerts | 10 min | `monitorSweep` | `worker/monitor.ts:124` |
| Outbound abuse detection | 10 min | `abuseSweep` | `worker/abuse.ts:16` |
| In-guest disk sampling | 10 min | `sampleServerDisks` | `worker/monitor.ts:68` |
| Scheduled backups | 15 min | `scheduledBackupSweep` | `worker/backup-schedule.ts:21` |
| Dedicated IP pool sync | 5 min | `syncDedicatedIpPool` | `worker/index.ts:1098` |
| Visitor geo enrichment | 90 s | `geoEnrichSweep` | `worker/geo.ts` |
| Game server auto-update | 6 h | `gameUpdateSweep` | `worker/game-update.ts:144` |

**Consequence you must internalise:** because sweeps share the loop with jobs, a long-running job
(a 40-minute migration, a large backup) delays every sweep behind it. Billing is not late because
it is broken; it is late because the worker is busy. Check `Job` before assuming a billing bug.

## Environments: production, staging and sandbox

Two complete copies of the platform run on one machine, plus a third mode (`SANDBOX`) that
changes behaviour rather than location.

| | Production | Staging |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Path | `/opt/nxeon` | `/opt/nxeon-staging` |
| Database | `nxeon` | `nxeon_staging` |
| Web unit / port | `nxeon-web` :3000 | `nxeon-staging-web` :3001 |
| Worker unit | `nxeon-worker` | `nxeon-staging-worker` |
| Console relay | `nxeon-console-proxy` :8899 | `nxeon-staging-console-proxy` :8898 |
| Terminal backend | `nxeon-terminal` :8901 | `nxeon-terminal-staging` :8902 |
| nginx ports | 80 / 443 | 8080 / 8443 |
| VM IP range | 10.20.0.100–250 | 10.20.0.50–99 |
| SSH port range | 20000–29999 | 30000–30999 |
| NAT chain | `NXEON_FWD` | `NXEON_FWD_STG` |
| Proxmox VM tag | `nxeon` | `nxeon-staging` |
| Stripe | live (`sk_live…`) | test (`sk_test…`) |
| Sandbox mode | off | on (`NXEON_SANDBOX=1`) |

**CORRECTION.** Earlier documentation said instance differences are driven entirely by `.env`
variables such as `NXEON_ENV`, `NXEON_COOKIE_NAME`, `NXEON_NAT_CHAIN`, `NXEON_TAG`,
`NXEON_IP_START/END` and `NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END`. That is true of **staging only**. The
production `.env` sets none of them — production runs on the code defaults, and staging overrides
them. The practical effect is identical, but if you go looking for `NXEON_TAG` in
`/opt/nxeon/.env` you will not find it, and that is not a misconfiguration.

**What `SANDBOX` actually does.** `lib/sandbox.ts` exports a `SANDBOX` boolean that every
side-effecting path checks. When it is on:

- The worker simulates every job. No Proxmox clone, config, resize or start. Synthetic vmids
  (`990000 + count`) and synthetic IPs (`sandboxIp(vmid)`) — `worker/index.ts:197`.
- Sweeps that would touch Proxmox or OVH are neutralised.
- Every SSH-executing subsystem (control panel, SSL, game config, migration, file manager)
  returns synthetic success instead of connecting.
- Billing still runs, on play money. Wallet debits behave exactly as in production.
- An instant wallet top-up bypasses Stripe.
- A persistent SANDBOX banner marks the environment.

Sandbox exists so that staging can exercise the real code paths, including the money paths,
without touching real infrastructure. Do not disable it on staging.

**The deploy pipeline.**

```
   local commit ──▶ .git/hooks/post-commit auto-pushes to GitHub
        │
        ▼
   scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]
        │  git fetch + checkout ref into /opt/nxeon-staging
        │  npm ci / npm run build
        │  npx prisma db push        ← additive schema sync
        │  systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
        │  health-check :8080
        ▼
   verify on staging (sandbox — no real VMs, play money)
        │
        ▼
   scripts/promote-production.sh
        │  build in /opt/nxeon
        │  systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker
        ▼
   production live
```

Staging-first is a hard rule for anything touching provisioning, money or SSH. See
"Runbook: deploying a change" for the safe procedure, especially the worker-restart check.

## Domains, TLS and routing

The platform's own hostnames are configured in exactly one file and nothing in application code
hardcodes a domain.

**Single source of truth:** `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` with four values — `BASE_DOMAIN`,
`ADMIN_HOST`, `STAGING_HOST`, `CERTBOT_EMAIL`. `scripts/configure-domains.sh` regenerates every
nginx vhost from it, obtains Let's Encrypt certificates over the webroot ACME challenge, wires
the rate-limit and websocket locations, sets `APP_URL` and `COOKIE_SECURE`, and reloads nginx.

**Current live state**, read from the machine:

| Setting | Value | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BASE_DOMAIN` | `nxeon.cloud` | Primary customer domain, own LE cert |
| `ADMIN_HOST` in domains.env | `4j3d7gkr2wcbi34.revsports.ca` | Legacy — see below |
| `NXEON_ADMIN_HOSTS` in `.env` | `4j3d7gkr2wcbi34.nxeon.cloud,4j3d7gkr2wcbi34.revsports.ca` | Both admin hosts accepted |
| `APP_URL` | `https://nxeon.cloud` | |
| `STAGING_HOST` | `staging.revsports.ca` | |
| nginx vhosts | `nxeon-cloud`, `nxeon-admin-cloud`, `nxeon`, `nxeon-mail`, `nxeon-staging`, `nxeon-staging-admin` | |

**CORRECTION.** Earlier documentation gave the customer portal as `https://revsports.ca`. The
primary domain is now `nxeon.cloud`; `revsports.ca` 301-redirects to it. Every URL in the old
header block was stale.

**Routing rules.**

- Customer portal on the apex. Requests to `/admin` on the public domain return **404**, so the
  admin panel's existence is not discoverable there.
- Admin ops portal on an unguessable subdomain; its root redirects to `/admin`.
- All HTTP is 301-redirected to HTTPS. Certificates auto-renew via the `certbot.timer` systemd
  timer.
- `/console-ws` and `/terminal-ws` are websocket-upgrade locations proxying to 8899 and 8901.
  They exist on the `nxeon-cloud` and `nxeon-admin-cloud` vhosts.

**GAP — the browser console is almost certainly broken in production.** `CONSOLE_PUBLIC_WS_URL`
in `/opt/nxeon/.env` is `wss://revsports.ca/console-ws`, and it is handed to the browser verbatim
by `app/api/console/[serverId]/route.ts:147`. But the `revsports.ca` 443 server block contains
only `location / { return 301 https://nxeon.cloud$request_uri; }` — there is no `/console-ws`
location on that host. Browsers do not follow redirects during a WebSocket handshake, so the
connection fails. **Fix:** set `CONSOLE_PUBLIC_WS_URL=wss://nxeon.cloud/console-ws` and restart
`nxeon-web`. This was found by reading the live config while writing this manual and has not been
applied — applying it is a production change and needs an owner decision.

## Infrastructure: host, storage, network

**The host.** One OVH KS-GAME dedicated machine — Intel i7-7700K (4 cores / 8 threads), 64 GB
RAM, public IP `51.79.162.96`, Proxmox node name `ns5002569`. This single box runs Proxmox, both
application stacks, PostgreSQL, nginx, the workers, the Mailcow VM and every customer VM.

**Storage — three ZFS pools chosen per workload.**

| Pool | Media | Usable | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vmdata` | 2×450 GB NVMe, mirrored | ~344 GB | Premium tier. Redundant. Default clone target. |
| `vmdata-hdd` | 1×4 TB HDD | ~3.6 TB | Bulk tier. Cheaper, slower, not mirrored. |
| `backup` (`/tank/backup`) | on the 4 TB pool | — | DB dumps, VM backups, cloud-init snippets, ISOs |

A plan's `storageTier` field (`nvme` or `hdd`) selects the pool at clone time —
`worker/index.ts:217`. The per-node override lives on `Node.storageNvme` / `Node.storageHdd`.

**Network — two bridges, two connectivity models.**

```
                       ┌──────────────────── vmbr0 (public bridge) ─────┐
   OVH failover IP ───▶│  VM with dedicated IPv4                        │
   + Virtual MAC       │  net0 = virtio=<vmac>,bridge=vmbr0             │
                       │  ipconfig0 = ip=<addr>/32,gw=51.79.162.254     │
                       └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘

                       ┌──────────────────── vmbr1 (NAT bridge) ────────┐
   host public IP ────▶│  10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1                      │
   :20000-29999 DNAT   │  VM gets 10.20.0.x, reaches internet via NAT   │
   ──────────────────▶ │  inbound SSH (and customer port forwards)      │
                       │  arrive as DNAT into the NXEON_FWD chain       │
                       └───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The DNAT chain is **rebuilt from the database** by `worker/network.ts:28` `syncPortForwards`,
called after every provision, delete, suspend, unsuspend and on worker start. Never hand-edit
the `NXEON_FWD` chain — your edit will be erased on the next sync, and the database will still
disagree with reality until then.

**Templates.** VMIDs 9000–9009 are cloud-init base images marked as Proxmox templates: Ubuntu
24.04 / 22.04 / 20.04, Debian 13 / 12 / 11, AlmaLinux 9 / 8, Rocky 9 / 8. Provisioning does a
full clone of one of these rather than installing an OS. **VMIDs 9000–9999 are reserved and must
never be touched** except to add a new template. The Mailcow VM is vmid 8000.

**Capacity.** `lib/capacity.ts` provides `capacityCheck` (RAM oversell guard) and
`diskCapacityCheck` (disk guard), both called by `placeOrder` at `lib/order.ts:164` and
`lib/order.ts:178`. `Node.capacityRamMB` defaults to 56000 — the RAM the platform is willing to
commit on a 64 GB box.

**Multi-node.** Each `Node` row carries its own Proxmox credentials, bridge, subnet prefix, IP
and port ranges, NAT chain and storage names. `lib/proxmox.ts` `pveFor(node)` returns a client
bound to those credentials, and `worker/index.ts:69` `nodeFor(server)` resolves the right one for
every handler, falling back to the primary node and then to the env-configured global client.
`lib/order.ts:85` `scheduleNode` picks the enabled ONLINE node with the most free RAM. One node
exists today; the code path for more is written and unexercised.

## Feature flags and environment variables

Every secret lives in `/opt/nxeon/.env` — `chmod 600`, gitignored, never in code, never sent to
the browser. `instrumentation.ts` validates required variables at boot.

**The four real-infrastructure gates.** These decide whether a subsystem SSHes into a customer's
machine or returns a safe simulation. All four are checked as `!SANDBOX && process.env.X === "1"`.

| Flag | Guards | Checked at | Production value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL` | Websites, databases, apps, cron, services | `worker/websites.ts:39` and peers | **ON** |
| `ENABLE_REAL_SSL` | certbot issuance on the customer VM | `worker/ssl.ts:303` | **off** (simulated) |
| `ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG` | Writing game config files over SSH | `worker/game-config.ts:39` | **off** (simulated) |

`ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION=1`" and that the control panel "requires `ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL=1` on prod".

**Capacity guards** (`lib/capacity.ts`): the RAM ceiling is
`(NXEON_HOST_RAM_MB − NXEON_HOST_RAM_RESERVE_MB) × NXEON_RAM_OVERSELL`, defaulting to
`(64000 − 8000) × 1.5 = 84000 MB`. Disk is **not** oversold: `NXEON_HOST_DISK_GB` (default 800)
× `NXEON_DISK_SAFETY` (default 0.9), preferring the live Proxmox storage total when readable.
An amber "near capacity" banner appears on the deploy page at 85% RAM utilisation.

**Failure modes.**

| Failure | What the customer sees | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plan or image deactivated mid-flow | "Plan or OS not available." | `lib/order.ts:108` |
| Plan too small for the image | "X needs at least N GB RAM and M GB disk — choose a larger plan." | `lib/order.ts:110` |
| Host out of RAM | "The host is at capacity — not enough RAM headroom…" | `lib/capacity.ts:78` |
| Host out of disk | "Not enough disk headroom on this node…" | `lib/capacity.ts:132` |
| Wallet short | "Insufficient balance." | `lib/order.ts:188` |
| Stripe not configured | "Card payments aren't set up yet — top up your wallet to deploy." | `lib/actions.ts:431` |
| Clone or start fails | Job retries up to 3 times, then `Server.status = ERROR` | `worker/index.ts:975` |
| Worker killed mid-provision | Reaper re-queues, or ERROR on the third attempt | `worker/index.ts:1000` |

**GAP — a terminally failed PROVISION is not refunded.** `reconcileFailedJob`
(`worker/index.ts:883`) handles only `DISK_EXPAND` and `RESIZE`. There is no `PROVISION` branch.
A customer whose first deploy fails three times keeps a `PAID` invoice, a debited wallet and a
server stuck in `ERROR`. Support must refund by hand via `/admin/users/[id]` → credit, and
delete the dead server. This is the single most likely support ticket at launch.

**GAP — the Review "paid but not provisioned" screen says nothing.** If `placeOrder` throws
inside `/api/stripe/confirm` the customer is redirected to `/dashboard/deploy?paid=1`
(`app/api/stripe/confirm/route.ts:38`), but the deploy page reads no search params at all, so
the customer sees a blank wizard with no explanation and money in their wallet. The same is true
of the Stripe `cancel_url` (`?canceled=1`).

**GAP — the Access step's "Root password" field is never submitted.** The state exists at
`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:124` but there is no hidden input for it and `OrderIntent`
has no such field (`lib/order.ts:39`). The root password is always machine-generated in
`provision()` (`worker/index.ts:222`). The helper text "Blank = we generate a strong one" is
accidentally accurate.

**GAP — card-paid deploys drop the deploy-time SSH key.** `createOrderCheckout` strips
`sshPublicKey` and `sshKeyName` before writing the Stripe metadata (`lib/stripe.ts:26`), so the
wallet path saves the key and the card path silently does not.

**Dead code.** `lib/actions.ts:233` `orderServer` is the original wallet-only order action. Its
only consumer, `components/OrderForm.tsx`, is rendered nowhere, and `/dashboard/order` redirects
to `/dashboard/deploy`. It lacks `extraDiskGB` handling and `diskCapacityCheck`. Do not treat it
as live and do not copy from it.

**How an admin diagnoses a deploy.**

1. `/admin/provisioning` — queued, running and failed-in-24h counts plus the last 30 failures.
2. `/admin/jobs` — the last 100 jobs with `attempts` and the truncated `error`.
3. `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -n 200` — the handler's own logging, prefixed `[worker]`.
4. `/admin/audit` filtered on `server.order`.
5. In the database: `SELECT status, attempts, error FROM "Job" WHERE "serverId" = '…' ORDER BY "createdAt";`

## Plans, terms, promos and pricing

**What it does.** Prices everything the platform sells. All of it is data or pure functions —
there are no prices in the provisioning code.

**Plans** live in the `Plan` table and are edited at `/admin/plans`. Current production rows:

| Slug | Name | vCPU | RAM | Disk | Bandwidth | Price | Tier | Active |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `nano` | Nano | 1 | 1 GB | 15 GB | 1 TB | $3.49/mo | nvme | no |
| `starter` | Starter | 1 | 2 GB | 25 GB | 1 TB | $8.99/mo | nvme | yes |
| `standard` | Standard | 2 | 4 GB | 50 GB | 2 TB | $12.99/mo | nvme | yes |
| `pro` | Pro | 3 | 8 GB | 80 GB | 4 TB | $20.99/mo | nvme | yes |
| `max` | Max | 4 | 16 GB | 120 GB | 8 TB | $32.99/mo | nvme | yes |

Dedicated IPv4 is folded into these prices (`dedicated_ip_price_cents` defaults to `0`), which is
why "dedicated IP included" is an honest claim.

**Terms and commitment discounts** — `lib/billing-terms.ts:9`, exactly four:

| Months | Label | Discount | Charge formula |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Monthly | 0% | `monthly × 1` |
| 12 | Annual | 10% | `round(monthly × 12 × 0.90)` |
| 24 | Biennial | 15% | `round(monthly × 24 × 0.85)` |
| 36 | Triennial | 20% | `round(monthly × 36 × 0.80)` |

Domains use a separate ladder — 1 year 0%, 2 years 5%, 3 years 10% (`lib/billing-terms.ts:33`).
`vpsTerm(months)` falls back to Monthly for any unrecognised value, so a tampered form cannot
invent a discount.

**Promos are intro discounts, not price changes.** `lib/promotions.ts` rotates seasonal promos
with a 15% "Launch Sale" fallback that is always active between windows, so `currentPromo` never
returns null (`:115`). The discount applies to the **plan line of the first term only**;
`worker/billing.ts` never calls `promoPriceCents`, so renewals bill the regular price. That is
why the strikethrough on the marketing pages is the genuine renewal price and the highlighted
price is the genuine first charge.

| Promo | Discount | Window (month-day) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New Year Sale | 30% | 01-01 → 01-07 |
| Valentine's Sale | 20% | 02-08 → 02-16 |
| Spring Sale | 25% | 03-20 → 04-05 |
| Summer Sale | 30% | 06-21 → 08-10 |
| Back-to-School Sale | 25% | 08-15 → 09-15 |
| Halloween Sale | 25% | 10-24 → 10-31 |
| Black Friday | 40% | 11-24 → 11-30 |
| Cyber Monday | 45% | 12-01 → 12-02 |
| Holiday Sale | 35% | 12-15 → 12-31 |
| Launch Sale (fallback) | 15% | any other date |

Promo windows resolve in **local server time**, not UTC (`lib/promotions.ts:68`). Add-ons —
dedicated IP and extra disk — are never discounted, by term or by promo.

**Displayed equals charged.** The wizard recomputes the same arithmetic client-side
(`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:96`) from the promo the server passed it. Any change to
the pricing maths must be made in the shared pure module, never in one side only. This is the
same discipline as `lib/wallet-split.ts` and `lib/extra-disk.ts`.

**Admin editing.** `adminSavePlan` (`lib/actions.ts:790`) is ADMIN-only and bounds every field:
`cpuCores` 1–8, `ramMB` 256–49152, `diskGB` 5–300, `bandwidthTB` 0.1–100, `priceCents` ≥ 0, slug
`^[a-z0-9-]+$`. It audits `admin.save_plan`.

**There is no price lock.** Renewals read `plan.priceCents` live (`worker/billing.ts:111`), so
editing a plan's price changes what every existing customer on that plan pays at their next
renewal. If you need to grandfather customers, clone the plan and move new signups to the new
row — do not edit the old one.

**Add-on prices are Settings, not plan fields**: `dedicated_ip_price_cents` (default `0`) and
`extra_disk_gb_price_cents` (default `10`, i.e. $0.10/GB/month).

## Wallet, checkout and the wallet/card split

**What it does.** Holds a prepaid balance in integer cents, and splits any charge between that
balance and a card so that the customer is never double-charged and the wallet is never touched
before the card clears.

**The screen** — the Review step of any purchase wizard.

```
┌─ Payment ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Due today                                  $188.29   │
│                                                       │
│  [x] Apply my balance  (you have $50.00)              │
│                                                       │
│      Wallet                                −$50.00    │
│      Card                                  $138.29    │
│      ─────────────────────────────────────────────    │
│      Charged now to your card              $138.29    │
│                                                       │
│  ⓘ Stripe's minimum charge is $0.50, so we leave      │
│    50¢ on the card and apply slightly less balance.   │
│    (only shown when the clamp fires)                  │
│                                                       │
│              [ Pay & deploy → ]                       │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**The split maths** — `lib/wallet-split.ts:33`, a pure module with no server-only imports so the
client and the server compute byte-identical numbers.

```
  walletSplit({ dueCents, balanceCents, useWallet })

  due <= 0                      → { wallet: 0,   card: 0 }
  useWallet = false             → { wallet: 0,   card: due }
  balance >= due                → { wallet: due, card: 0 }        no Stripe at all
  balance <  due                → { wallet: balance, card: due − balance }

  then, the Stripe floor (STRIPE_MIN_CENTS = 50):
  if 0 < card < 50 and due >= 50 → { wallet: due − 50, card: 50, clamped: true }
```

**The charge sequence, and why it cannot double-charge.**

```
  1. Stripe Checkout is created for cardCents ONLY.          lib/stripe.ts:19
     The wallet is NOT debited at this point.
  2. Customer pays. Stripe redirects to /api/stripe/confirm.
  3. creditCheckoutSession(sessionId)                        lib/stripe.ts:192
       · requires session.payment_status === "paid"
       · INSERT WalletTransaction { stripeSessionId }  ← UNIQUE
       · P2002 duplicate key ⇒ return false ⇒ "already credited"
       · in the same $transaction: increment balance, notify, write a PAID invoice
  4. Only if credited === true does the route call placeOrder /
     applyResize / applyDiskExpand, which debits the FULL charge.
       net effect: card paid cardCents, existing balance absorbed walletApplied.
```

The idempotency key is the database constraint `WalletTransaction.stripeSessionId @unique`
(`prisma/schema.prisma:379`), not a read-then-write. A replayed confirm URL, a duplicate webhook
delivery, and a confirm racing its own webhook all converge on exactly one credit.

**`debitWallet`** (`lib/wallet.ts:16`) is a single conditional statement —
`UPDATE "User" SET balanceCents = balanceCents − ? WHERE id = ? AND balanceCents >= ?` — and
throws `InsufficientBalanceError` when zero rows match. Two concurrent charges therefore cannot
drive a balance negative, and because the call sits inside the caller's `$transaction`, the throw
rolls back the row and the job it would have paid for.

**Top-ups.** `/api/stripe/checkout` requires a session, rejects amounts above $5000 or
non-finite, and enforces the `min_topup_cents` setting (default 500). The demo gateway
`topUp` (`lib/actions.ts:489`) is hard-refused when `NODE_ENV === "production"` and again when
Stripe is configured, and is rate-limited to 10 per hour per user and IP. It exists only so
staging can add play money.

**Webhook.** `/api/stripe/webhook` verifies the Stripe signature with `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and
handles only `checkout.session.completed`, calling the same idempotent credit.

**Failure modes.**

| Failure | Effect | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Customer closes the Stripe tab | No charge, no job | Retry the wizard |
| Confirm route throws after credit | Money in wallet, nothing provisioned | Customer re-runs the wizard; the balance covers it |
| Price drifts between checkout and confirm | `placeOrder` re-quotes and can exceed the paid amount → wallet debit fails | Customer keeps the credit; support completes the order manually |
| Stripe metadata over 490 chars | `JSON.parse` throws, is swallowed, intent returns null, customer is credited but nothing is ordered | Latent — typical intents are ~250 chars |

**GAP — no price is pinned into the Stripe session.** `placeOrder` re-runs `orderQuote` at
confirm time, re-reading `currentPromo(new Date())`, the add-on settings and `plan.priceCents`.
If a promo window closes between checkout and confirm, or an admin edits a price, the charge can
exceed what the customer agreed to and the order silently fails to a credited wallet.

**GAP — subscription renewals have no card auto-charge.** This is the largest known billing hole
and is documented in full in "Renewals, grace, suspension and termination".

**How an admin diagnoses it.** `/admin/billing` shows the wallet ledger with search by
description or email, 30-day and lifetime charge sums, and total customer liability. The
authoritative cross-check is: **a Stripe session with `payment_status = paid` and no matching
`WalletTransaction.stripeSessionId` row is an uncredited payment.** Query:

```sql
SELECT id, "userId", "amountCents", description, "stripeSessionId", "createdAt"
FROM "WalletTransaction"
WHERE "stripeSessionId" IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY "createdAt" DESC LIMIT 50;
```

**Code entry points.**

| Thing | Symbol | Location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create data (pure, for use inside a transaction) | `invoiceCreateData` | `lib/invoices.ts:72` |
| Create directly | `createInvoice` | `lib/invoices.ts:104` |

**Invariant.** `amountCents` is always derived — the sum of `lineItems[].amountCents` plus
`taxCents` (`lib/invoices.ts:81`). A caller cannot desync the total from the lines. `paidAt` is
set only when `status === "PAID"`.

**Every charge path writes a PAID invoice inside its own guarded transaction:**

| Charge | Location |
| --- | --- |
| New VPS order | `lib/order.ts:211` |
| Wallet top-up | `lib/stripe.ts:230` |
| VPS auto-renewal | `worker/billing.ts:146` |
| Manual "Renew now" | `lib/actions.ts:643` |
| Domain auto-renewal | `worker/billing.ts:539` |
| Email subscription renewal | `worker/product-renewals.ts:173` |
| Volume renewal | `worker/product-renewals.ts:351` |

**Admin actions.** `generateInvoiceForServer` creates an **OPEN** invoice for one 30-day period
and does **not** charge the wallet — it is a billing document, not a payment. `voidInvoice`
refuses a PAID invoice ("refund instead"); `markInvoicePaid` refuses a VOID one.
`regenerateMissingInvoices` backfills OPEN invoices for paid servers that have none.

**GAP — `regenerateMissingInvoices` dedupes on a hostname substring.** It looks for a non-VOID
invoice whose `description` contains the hostname (`lib/actions-billing.ts:98`). Hostnames like
`web` and `web2` therefore collide and the backfill silently skips one of them. Do not rely on
this for reconciliation; use the `WalletTransaction` ledger.

**GAP — `invoice_prefix` is never read.** The setting exists (`lib/settings.ts:38`, default
`"INV-"`) and is editable in the admin, but `renderInvoiceHTML` hardcodes
`#${String(number).padStart(5,"0")}` (`lib/invoices.ts:147`), as do both detail pages. Changing
the prefix does nothing.

**GAP — tax is never applied.** `lib/tax.ts:74` reads the `tax_percent` setting, but no charge
path passes `taxCents` to `invoiceCreateData`. Every invoice ships `taxCents: 0` and renders
`Tax $0.00`. If the business needs to charge tax before launch, this is unbuilt, not misconfigured.

**GAP — no PDF library.** The download route returns branded print-ready HTML with a print
stylesheet and a "Print / Save as PDF" button (`lib/invoices.ts:255`). Earlier documentation
described "invoice HTML/PDF rendering", which overstates it. Access control on the route is
correct: 401 unauthenticated, 404 missing, 403 when neither owner nor ADMIN, and
`Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

**How an admin diagnoses it.** `/admin/invoices` (status filter, 25 per page, bulk void),
`/admin/invoices/[id]`, CSV via `/api/admin/export?type=invoices`, and the `AuditLog` actions
`invoice.generate`, `invoice.void`, `invoice.mark_paid`, `invoice.regenerate_missing`.

## Renewals, grace, suspension and termination

**What it does.** Charges the wallet when a server's term ends, warns, gives grace, suspends,
warns again, and finally deletes. It is the only part of the platform that destroys customer
data on a timer, so read the state machine carefully.

**The state machine** — all times relative to `Server.expiresAt`. `isFree` servers are exempt
everywhere.

```
   T−3d ──────────────── T+0 ─────── T+3d ──────────────── T+11d ─── T+13d
    │                     │            │                      │        │
    │                     │            │                      │        │
 "renews soon —      renewal attempt  GRACE ENDS          "will be   TERMINATE
  action needed"     (auto-renew on)  → SUSPEND            deleted    → status DELETING
  notification       CAS on expiresAt    Job                soon"     → Job DELETE
  (only if           debitWallet         suspendedNote      notif.    → all data gone
   autoRenew off     WalletTransaction   notification       (deduped  → dedicated IP
   OR balance        PAID Invoice                            2 days)     released
   short)            AuditLog
                     billing.renewed
                        │
                        └─ InsufficientBalanceError → fall through to grace
```

| Constant | Env var | Default | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Grace days | `NXEON_GRACE_DAYS` | 3 | `worker/billing.ts:27` |
| Terminate days after grace | `NXEON_TERMINATE_DAYS` | 10 | `worker/billing.ts:31` |
| Warn before terminate | `NXEON_WARN_BEFORE_TERMINATE_DAYS` | 2 | `worker/billing.ts:33` |
| Domain renew window | — | 7 days | `worker/billing.ts:29` |

None of these are set in the production `.env`, so production runs on the defaults: suspend at
expiry + 3 days, warn at + 11 days, delete at + 13 days.

**The renewal price** (`worker/billing.ts:101`):

```
   game server  →  gamePlan.priceCents                    (flat, per its own term)
   otherwise    →  vpsTermPriceCents(plan.priceCents, termMonths)
                 + (dedicatedIp ? ipMonthly × months : 0)   ← off the DedicatedIp ROW,
                 + extraDiskGB × extra_disk_gb_price_cents     not the intent flag
                   × months
```

Billing the IP surcharge off the `DedicatedIp` relation rather than `Server.wantsDedicatedIp` is
deliberate: a server that fell back to NAT because the pool was empty must not be charged forever
for an address it never received.

**Double-charge protection.** Every renewal path uses a compare-and-swap on `expiresAt`:

```
  UPDATE "Server" SET "expiresAt" = <new> WHERE id = ? AND "expiresAt" = <old>
  count === 0  →  throw AlreadyRenewedError  →  rolls back the debit,
                  the WalletTransaction and the Invoice
```

`worker/billing.ts:129`, mirrored in `renewNow` (`lib/actions.ts:627`), the email renewal
(`worker/product-renewals.ts:156`) and the volume renewal (`worker/product-renewals.ts:335`). The
sweep deliberately does **not** gate on the `balanceCents` it read at the top of the loop — that
snapshot goes stale the moment the first renewal debits — and relies on `debitWallet` re-checking
atomically.

**Manual renewal.** `renewNow` (`lib/actions.ts:590`) recomputes the identical price, pre-checks
the balance ("Insufficient balance — top up your wallet first."), runs the same CAS transaction,
clears `suspendedNote`, and unsuspends a SUSPENDED server after payment. On a lost CAS race it
returns "This server was just renewed — refresh to see the new expiry."

**Domain auto-renewal** (`worker/billing.ts:460`) renews within 7 days of expiry when the owner
opted in and has funds. The registrar call happens **before** the wallet debit, so a debit
failure after a successful registrar renewal is recorded as
`AuditLog action = "domain.renew.uncharged"` and logged as `[billing] UNCHARGED domain renewal`.
That is money owed by the customer that must be collected manually — grep for it periodically.

**Add-on product renewals** (`worker/product-renewals.ts:520`) handle business email and volumes
in four phases, each phase and each row individually try/caught so one poison row cannot abort
the sweep. Enforcement is deliberately **non-destructive**: an unpaid email subscription becomes
`SUSPENDED` with its mailboxes intact; an unpaid volume is `DETACHED` with its data intact.
`nextExpiry` bases on `max(currentExpiry, now)` so a long-expired item is brought forward with a
single charge and never back-billed.

**GAP — the admin's dunning settings are not wired to anything.** `dunning_grace_days` (3),
`dunning_warn_days` (7), `dunning_terminate_days` (14) and `auto_suspend_enabled` (true) exist in
`lib/settings.ts:39-42`, are editable at `/admin/settings` → Billing, and are persisted — but a
repo-wide search finds **zero reads** outside the settings module, the save action and the panel
itself. The worker uses only the `NXEON_*` environment variables. **The panel advertises a 7/14
day schedule while the worker actually runs 3/13, and turning off "Auto-suspend overdue accounts"
does nothing.** Verified by exhaustive grep while writing this manual.

**GAP — servers in `ERROR`, `PENDING` or `PROVISIONING` are invisible to billing.** Both the warn
query (`worker/billing.ts:58`) and the due query (`worker/billing.ts:94`) filter
`status IN ("RUNNING","STOPPED")`. A server stuck in `ERROR` past its expiry is never renewed,
never warned, never suspended and never terminated — it runs indefinitely, unbilled. Audit for
this with:

```sql
SELECT id, hostname, status, "expiresAt" FROM "Server"
WHERE "isFree" = false AND "expiresAt" < now()
  AND status NOT IN ('RUNNING','STOPPED');
```

**GAP — renewals debit the wallet only; there is no card auto-charge.** `worker/billing.ts`
charges via `debitWallet`; on `InsufficientBalanceError` it falls through to grace and then
suspends. There is no saved-card path anywhere: no `setup_future_usage`, no SetupIntent, no
`off_session` PaymentIntent. `User.stripePaymentMethodId` exists in the schema and is never
written and never read. `User.autoRechargeEnabled` / `autoRechargeThresholdCents` /
`autoRechargeAmountCents` are settable through `lib/actions-billing-prefs.ts` but **nothing calls
that action and nothing consumes those columns**. Consequence: a customer with a perfectly good
card is suspended when their wallet empties. Six dunning email templates exist on `emails.*`
(`paymentReceipt`, `paymentFailed`, `paymentRetryFailed`, `paymentActionRequired`,
`paymentFinalNotice`, `cardExpiringSoon`); the charging engine itself is not built.

**How an admin diagnoses it.**

- `/admin/subscriptions` for the fleet view; `/admin/servers/[id]` for one server's `expiresAt`,
  `isFree`, `autoRenew` and `suspendedNote`.
- `/admin/audit` filtered on `billing.renewed`, `billing.suspended_unpaid`,
  `billing.terminated_unpaid`, `billing.volume_detached_unpaid`, `domain.renew.uncharged`.
- `journalctl -u nxeon-worker | grep -E '\[billing\]|\[product-billing\]'`.
- "Billing did not run" is far more often "the worker was busy with a long job" than a bug —
  check `Job` for a `RUNNING` row first.
