## SSL certificates

**What it does.** Requests a Let's Encrypt certificate for a customer's domain and installs it on
their VPS.

**GAP — this is simulated in production right now.** `ENABLE_REAL_SSL` is not set in
`/opt/nxeon/.env`, so `sslIssue` (`worker/ssl.ts:281`) takes the default branch at `:322`, marks
the certificate `ACTIVE` with `issuedAt = now` and `expiresAt = now + 90 days`, and notifies the
customer "Your Let's Encrypt certificate is active and valid for 90 days (sandbox)". **No
certificate is issued and nothing is installed on the VM.** A customer looking at
`/dashboard/ssl` sees certificates that do not exist. This is the highest-severity honesty gap in
the platform and must be resolved before launch — either by enabling the flag after testing on a
throwaway VM, or by hiding the feature.

**The screen** — `/dashboard/ssl`.

```
┌─ SSL certificates ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Request a certificate                                                        │
│   Domain [ example.com        ]  Server [ web1 ▾ ]      [ Request ]           │
│   ⓘ The domain must already point at this server — Let's Encrypt verifies     │
│     ownership over HTTP on port 80.                                           │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Domain          Server   Status     Issued       Expires      Auto-renew     │
│  example.com     web1     ● ACTIVE   2026-07-20   2026-10-18   [ on ]  [Del]  │
│  api.example.com web1     ◐ ISSUING  —            —            [ on ]         │
│  old.example.com web1     ✕ FAILED   —            —            [ on ]  [Del]  │
│    ↳ "DNS for old.example.com does not resolve to this server"                │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Workflow.**

```
   requestCertificate(domain, serverId)          lib/actions-ssl.ts:51
        │  requireUser + ownership
        │  hostname validation
        │  SslCertificate { status: PENDING }
        │  Job SSL_ISSUE { certId }
        ▼
   sslIssue(job)                                 worker/ssl.ts:281
        │  status = ISSUING                                        :289
        │  realIssuanceEnabled = !SANDBOX && ENABLE_REAL_SSL==="1" :303
        │
        ├── false (production today) → status = ACTIVE, synthetic 90-day expiry
        │
        └── true → issueRealCertificate(cert)
              1. command -v certbot; install via apt-get or dnf if missing  :206
              2. verify the domain resolves to this server (clear message
                 rather than letting certbot fail cryptically)              :236
              3. certbot certonly --standalone -n --agree-tos -m <email> -d <domain>
              4. read the real notAfter back → issuedAt / expiresAt
        ▼
   status = ACTIVE (or FAILED with lastError) + notification
```

`--standalone` means certbot binds port 80 itself, so **the customer's web server must be stopped
or not yet listening**. That is a meaningful constraint compared with the webroot method the
migration engine uses.

**Data model.** `SslCertificate` — `domain`, `serverId`, `status`
(`PENDING | ISSUING | ACTIVE | FAILED | EXPIRED`), `issuer`, `autoRenew`, `lastError`, `issuedAt`,
`expiresAt`. Note `serverId` is a plain id with **no cascade**, so deleting a server leaves the
certificate rows behind.

**GAP — nothing renews these.** `autoRenew` is stored and never acted on: there is no sweep that
re-issues an `SslCertificate` approaching `expiresAt`, and no transition to `EXPIRED`. On a real
issuance the certbot systemd timer inside the customer's VM would handle renewal, but the
platform's own record would go stale.

**Issuing a certificate by hand** is covered in "Runbook: issuing a certificate by hand".

---

## Game servers and per-game configuration

**What it does.** Sells game servers as their own product with their own price tiers, and lets the
customer configure the game from the portal.

**The product.** `GamePlan` rows (14 seeded) each carry `gameFamily`, `ramMB`, `cpuCores`,
`diskGB`, `slots`, `priceCents`, `termMonths`, a `basePlanId` (the VPS `Plan` used to size and
provision the VM) and an `osTemplateId` (the game's image). Managed at `/admin/game-plans`;
customers order at `/dashboard/games`. Renewals charge `gamePlan.priceCents` flat
(`worker/billing.ts:103`), and game orders run the same `capacityCheck` a VPS order does.

Families: `minecraft`, `valheim`, `rust`, `palworld`, `cs2`, `terraria` (`lib/games.ts:3`).

**The screen** — the Game settings section on the server detail page, shown only when
`server.gamePlanId` is set.

```
┌─ Game settings ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Server type   ( ) Vanilla  (•) Paper  ( ) Purpur  ( ) Fabric  ( ) Forge      │
│                                                                               │
│  ┌─ Gameplay ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│  │  Difficulty        [ normal ▾ ]        server.properties: difficulty │      │
│  │  Game mode         [ survival ▾ ]      server.properties: gamemode   │      │
│  │  Max players       [ 20        ]       server.properties: max-players│      │
│  │  PvP               [x]                 server.properties: pvp        │      │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│  ┌─ World ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│  │  Seed              [              ]    Level type [ default ▾ ]     │      │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
│                                                       [ Save & apply ]        │
│  ⚠ Applying restarts the game server.                                         │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Auto-update    [ on ]   checked every 6 hours     [ Update now ]             │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**The schema is data, not code branches.** `lib/game-config.ts` defines one schema per family —
`MINECRAFT` (`:69`), `RUST` (`:176`), `VALHEIM` (`:241`), `CS2` (`:299`), `PALWORLD` (`:361`) —
registered in a map at `:437`. Each schema lists the server variants and the settings fields,
keyed on the game's **real** config keys (`server.properties`, `PalWorldSettings.ini`, cvars,
launch args — no invented cvars), typed enum/bool/int/string, with a deploy-or-live phase. Helpers:
`familyFor`, `schemaFor`, `validateConfig`. Terraria has a `GamePlan` family but no config schema.

**Workflow.** `getGameConfig` (`lib/actions-game-config.ts:58`) returns variant, config and schema
for an owned server. `saveGameConfig` (`:84`) validates against the schema, persists
`Server.gameVariant` and `Server.gameConfig`, and enqueues `GAME_CONFIG` — refused while another
job is in flight, mirroring the rest of the lifecycle.

**GAP — the apply is simulated in production.** `gameConfigApply` (`worker/game-config.ts:52`)
gates the real path on `REAL_APPLY_ENABLED = !SANDBOX && ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG === "1"` (`:39`),
which is **not set in production**. The default path stamps an applied-marker onto `gameConfig`
and notifies the user. **The customer's settings are saved and displayed but never written to the
game server.** The real implementation exists — it SSHes in, writes the config files and makes a
best-effort RCON call — and is off by default deliberately, but the customer-facing copy does not
distinguish the two.

**Auto-update.** `Server.autoUpdate` opts a game server into `gameUpdateSweep`
(`worker/game-update.ts:144`), which runs every 6 hours and enqueues `GAME_UPDATE`, handled by
`gameUpdate` (`:81`). `toggleAutoUpdate` (`lib/actions-server-ops.ts:46`) and `triggerGameUpdate`
(`:69`) are the customer controls.

**How an admin diagnoses it.** `/admin/games` for the catalog images, `/admin/game-plans` for the
tiers, `/admin/jobs` for `GAME_CONFIG` and `GAME_UPDATE` jobs. `Server.gameConfig` in the database
holds the saved values and the applied-marker.

---

## Web console (noVNC)

**What it does.** Puts the VM's actual screen in the browser — the only way in when SSH is broken
or the server will not boot.

```
   Browser                Next.js                console-proxy.mjs        Proxmox
      │                      │                        :8899                  │
      │ GET /api/console/<serverId>                                          │
      ├─────────────────────▶│ requireUser + ownership                       │
      │                      │ POST …/qemu/<vmid>/vncproxy ────────────────▶ │
      │                      │◀──────────── { port, ticket } ─────────────── │
      │                      │ mint a JWE: { node, vmid, port, vncticket,    │
      │                      │   tokenId, tokenSecret }                      │
      │                      │   alg dir · enc A256GCM · jti · exp 60s       │
      │◀── { wsPath, ticketId } ──────────────┤                              │
      │                                                                      │
      │ wss://HOST/console-ws?sid=<JWE>                                       │
      ├──────────────── nginx upgrade ───────▶│                              │
      │                                       │ decrypt, single-use check     │
      │                                       ├─ pipe to …/vncwebsocket ────▶│
      │◀═══════════ noVNC framebuffer ════════╪══════════════════════════════│
```

**The Proxmox ticket never reaches the browser.** The JWE is encrypted with a key derived from
`AUTH_SECRET`, is single-use, and expires in 60 seconds. The noVNC client is vendored at
`public/novnc` (1.4.0) so the tab works with no CDN.

**Code:** route `app/api/console/[serverId]/route.ts` (the JWE mint at `:136`, the public URL at
`:147`), relay `scripts/console-proxy.mjs` under `nxeon-console-proxy.service` on 8899.

**GAP — broken in production.** See "Domains, TLS and routing": `CONSOLE_PUBLIC_WS_URL` points at
`wss://revsports.ca/console-ws`, and that host has no such location — only a blanket 301. Set it
to `wss://nxeon.cloud/console-ws`.

**How an admin diagnoses it.** `systemctl status nxeon-console-proxy`, then
`journalctl -u nxeon-console-proxy -f` while the customer clicks Console. A 301 or 404 in the
browser's network tab on the `/console-ws` request is the symptom of the URL problem above; a
clean upgrade followed by an immediate close is usually an expired or replayed `sid`.

---

## Web terminal and the terminal dock

**What it does.** A real root shell on the customer's VM, in the portal, as a slide-in dock with
tabs — the thing that makes "run `claude` on your server" a two-click operation.

```
   Browser                Next.js               terminal-server            Guest VM
      │                      │                      :8901                     │
      │ POST /api/terminal/token { serverId }                                 │
      ├─────────────────────▶│ requireUser                                    │
      │                      │ ownership + status === RUNNING                 │
      │                      │ mint JWE { userId, serverId }, 60s             │
      │                      │   key = AUTH_SECRET + terminal-specific salt   │
      │                      │   (distinct from the console key)              │
      │◀── { token } ────────┤                                                │
      │ wss://HOST/terminal-ws?token=…                                        │
      ├──────── nginx ──────▶│                                                │
      │                      │ RE-VERIFY the token                            │
      │                      │ RE-CHECK ownership + RUNNING against the DB    │
      │                      │ connectionTarget(server) → host, port          │
      │                      │ serverRootPassword(server) → decrypt           │
      │                      │ ssh2 PTY shell ──────────────────────────────▶ │
      │◀═════════════ bytes both ways ════════╪═══════════════════════════════│
```

**The root password never crosses the websocket and is never logged.** The terminal backend is a
standalone `tsx` process (`terminal-server/index.ts`), deliberately **not** bundled by Next, so
the web process never loads ssh2.

**Limits:** 15 s to authenticate and connect, 10 minutes idle, 60 minutes hard cap. Resize is
handled. In SANDBOX no SSH is opened — a simulated echo shell is piped so staging works.

**The dock.** `components/customer/terminal/TerminalDock.tsx` plus a `TerminalDockProvider`
mounted in the portal `Shell`, so a shell session survives in-portal navigation. Multi-server tabs
(the "+" picker lists RUNNING servers via `lib/actions-terminal.ts:15` `listTerminalServers`) and a
minimise-to-widget mode that keeps the session live. xterm and WebSocket instances live in a ref
`Map` and are never recreated; switching tabs or minimising only toggles CSS.

**Deploy artifacts:** `deploy/nxeon-terminal.service`, `deploy/nxeon-terminal.nginx.txt`. Staging
runs `nxeon-terminal-staging.service` on 8902.

**How an admin diagnoses it.** `journalctl -u nxeon-terminal -f`. "Connects then immediately
closes" is almost always the ownership or RUNNING re-check failing on the backend, or a wrong
decrypted root password after a manual password change inside the VM.

---

## SFTP and the file manager

**What it does.** Browse, upload, download, edit, rename, delete and chmod files on the customer's
own VM, from the portal, with no SFTP client.

**The screen** — the Files tab.

```
┌─ Files ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  /var/www/example.com                              [ ↑ Up ] [ Upload ] [ New ]│
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Name                        Size      Modified            Perms   Actions    │
│  📁 wp-admin                 —         2026-07-12 09:14    755     [ open ]   │
│  📁 wp-content               —         2026-07-20 22:01    755     [ open ]   │
│  📄 wp-config.php            3.1 KB    2026-07-12 09:14    640     [edit][…]  │
│  📄 index.php                405 B     2026-07-12 09:14    644     [edit][…]  │
│                                                    … rename · chmod · delete  │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ┌─ wp-config.php ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐      │
│  │  <?php                                                              │      │
│  │  define( 'DB_NAME', 'appdb' );                                      │      │
│  │  …                                                       [ Save ]   │      │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**How it works.** `lib/sftp.ts` is a server-side `ssh2-sftp-client` proxy to the customer's own VM,
connecting with the server's decrypted root credential (the same `serverRootPassword` helper the
worker and the terminal use). `lib/actions-files.ts` exposes the operations, and
`app/api/files/[serverId]` streams uploads and downloads. Guards: ownership, **path-traversal
rejection**, and size caps. On staging the filesystem is simulated.

The types live in `lib/files-types.ts` rather than the action file — a `"use server"` module may
only export async functions, and exporting a type from one produced the "found object" error at
action-invocation time. The same constraint put `BACKUP_INTERVAL_CHOICES` in
`lib/backup-intervals.ts` and `GAME_FAMILIES` in `lib/games.ts`. **If you add a constant or type
next to a server action, you will break that action at runtime, not at build time.**

**Failure modes.** The tab requires the server to be RUNNING and reachable over SSH. A changed
root password inside the VM breaks it exactly as it breaks the terminal — reset it from the
Overview tab so the platform's copy matches.

---

## Domains: registration, DNS and transfers

**What it does.** Sells, renews, transfers and manages domain names through **name.com API v4**,
at a configurable markup over wholesale.

**CORRECTION — the registrar is name.com, not Namecheap.** `CLAUDE.md` documents
`lib/namecheap.ts` and `NAMECHEAP_*` variables. That file does not exist. The client is
`lib/registrar.ts`, HTTP Basic auth with `NAMECOM_USERNAME:NAMECOM_TOKEN` against
`https://api.name.com` (or `https://api.dev.name.com` when `NAMECOM_ENV=dev`), 30-second timeout.
`Domain.registrar` still defaults to `"namecheap"` in the schema (`prisma/schema.prisma:202`)
although every write path sets `"name.com"`.

**The markup maths.**

```
   domainMarkupPct()   = DOMAIN_MARKUP_PCT env, DEFAULT 25         registrar.ts:64
   retailCents(cost)   = round(cost × (1 + pct/100))                        :69
   customer pays       = domainTermPriceCents(retail, years)   ← term discount applies
   we pay name.com     = costCents × years                     ← NO term discount
   margin              = the difference, and BOTH numbers live on the Domain row
```

Term discounts: 1 year 0%, 2 years 5%, 3 years 10%. Transfers are always priced at the TLD's
**renewal** rate and always add exactly 1 year.

**The screens.**

```
  /dashboard/domains/register
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Find a domain    [ mycoolsite                     ]  [ Search ]              │
│   ● mycoolsite.com     available            $16.24/yr    [ Register ]         │
│   ✕ mycoolsite.net     taken                                                  │
│   ● mycoolsite.dev     available            $18.74/yr    [ Register ]         │
│  ── Term ──  (•) 1 year  ( ) 2 years −5%  ( ) 3 years −10%                    │
│  ── Registrant contact ── name / org / addr / city / state / zip / country     │
│     phone must be +CC.NNNNNNN                                                 │
│  ── Review ──  $16.24 due today          [ Register domain ]                  │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  /dashboard/domains/[id]
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  example.com  ● ACTIVE     registered 2026-01-14   expires 2027-01-14         │
│  Auto-renew [ on ]   Registrar lock [ on ]   WHOIS privacy [ on ]             │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  DNS records                                        [ Import ] [ Export CSV ] │
│   Type  Host         Value                   TTL    Prio                      │
│   A     @            51.79.162.181           300    —      [ delete ]         │
│   A     www          51.79.162.181           300    —      [ delete ]         │
│   MX    @            mail.nxeon.cloud        3600   10     [ delete ]         │
│   Add: [A ▾] [ host ] [ value ] [ 300 ] [ prio ]        [ Add record ]        │
│  Quick setup: [ Point at my server ] [ Reset to defaults ]                    │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  URL forwarding   host [ old ] → [ https://…  ]  [301 ▾]  [ Save ]            │
│  Transfer out     EPP/auth code   ••••••••   [ Reveal ]                       │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Registration** — `purchaseDomain` (`lib/actions-domains.ts:92`). Guards in order: `requireUser`,
the `feature_domains` flag, `registrarConfigured()`, `DOMAIN_RE`, a zod registrant contact
(phone `^\+\d{1,3}\.\d{4,14}$`), an in-process duplicate guard for 120 seconds, existing-row
checks, a live `checkDomains` (available, not premium, priced), and the balance check. The charge
transaction re-checks for duplicates inside the transaction, debits, writes the
`WalletTransaction`, and creates the `Domain` row as `PENDING`. Then it calls the registrar.

**The failure ladder is the interesting part.** `verifyRegistration` (`:76`) runs before any
refund decision:

| Verdict | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `registered` | Keep the charge, mark ACTIVE, stamp `error: "Recovered after registrar error: …"`, audit `domain.register.recovered`, notify |
| `not-registered` | Refund in a transaction (credit + `WalletTransaction` + `status: FAILED`), tell the customer "Registration failed: … (you were refunded)." |
| `unknown` | Stays PENDING **and charged**, `error: "NEEDS REVIEW — registrar status unconfirmed: …"`, audit `domain.register.needs_review`, notification "Domain … needs review", and the customer is told **not to retry** because they will not be charged twice |

**The `unknown` verdict is a manual queue.** Grep the audit log for
`domain.register.needs_review` regularly; each one is a domain that may or may not exist and a
customer who has been charged.

**Renewal** — `renewDomainAction` (`:279`). `RENEW_SLACK_MS` is 30 days (`:277`): if the
registrar's expiry already exceeds ours by more than that, the renewal is treated as already done
and the registrar call is skipped. If the registrar renewed but the debit failed, the outcome is
audited as `domain.renew.uncharged` — money owed, collect manually.

**DNS.** `ownedDomain` requires owner-or-admin **and** `status === ACTIVE`. Record types:
`A AAAA CNAME TXT MX NS SRV ALIAS`; TTL 60–86400, default 300; `@` or blank means the apex;
MX and SRV default to priority 10. `pointDomainAtServer` (`:459`) deletes existing apex and `www`
A records then adds both at TTL 300 — it requires the `PUBLIC_IP` environment variable.

Bulk and import (`lib/actions-domains-dns.ts`): `addDnsRecordsBulk` caps at 100 records per
request and dedupes against live records, returning `{added, skipped, failed}`. `parseDnsImport`
accepts `name,type,value[,ttl[,priority]]` with comma or whitespace separators and `#`/`;`
comments. `resetDnsToDefaults` deletes `A AAAA CNAME TXT MX SRV ALIAS` — **NS delegation is left
alone** — and re-adds `A @` plus `A www` at `PUBLIC_IP`.

**Redirects and registrar lock degrade honestly.** When the registrar is unavailable or
unconfigured, both persist the customer's **intent** into the `Setting` table under
`domain-redirect:<domainId>` / `domain-lock:<domainId>` and say so in the UI rather than pretending
the change landed.

**Transfer-in** — `lib/actions-domains-transfer.ts`. The revenue-generating counterpart to
transfer-out.

```
   quoteTransferIn(domain)                       :68
     · feature flag, transfersAvailable(), rate limit 20/60s
     · refuses a domain on another account, or already TRANSFER_PENDING
        │
        ▼
   Wizard: domain check → FOUR-ITEM PRE-FLIGHT GATE the customer must tick
        and the server re-validates:
          ackUnlocked  unlocked at the current registrar
          ackPrivacy   WHOIS privacy off / auth code obtainable
          ackAge       >60 days since registration or last transfer (ICANN, not policy)
          ackApproval  able to approve the confirmation email
        → auth code → review + submit
        │
        ▼
   submitTransferIn(...)                         :131
     · assertNotImpersonating, rate limit 5/10min
     · SERVER-SIDE RE-QUOTE — the client's price is never trusted;
       a drift aborts with "The registrar's price changed… Nothing has been charged."
     · REGISTRAR FIRST, MONEY SECOND:
         createTransfer() succeeds
           → ONE $transaction: row write (CAS or create) + debit +
             WalletTransaction + PAID Invoice
         createTransfer() fails
           → "The registrar refused the transfer: … (you were not charged)."
     · if the DEBIT fails after a successful submit → cancel at the registrar
       and audit domain.transfer_in.uncharged
        │
        ▼
   domainTransferInSweep()      worker/billing.ts:251, every ~10 min
     completed → ACTIVE, dates from domainInfo, auth code scrubbed
     failed    → TRANSFER_FAILED with the registrar's reason, wallet credited back
     pending   → refresh the raw status, nudge the customer every 3 days to approve
                 the LOSING registrar's email
```

**Charging for an unsubmitted transfer is structurally impossible.** Double-charging is blocked by
the in-process submit guard, the UNIQUE `Domain.name` (or a compare-and-swap off the retried row's
status) inside the charging transaction, and name.com refusing a second in-flight transfer.
Settlement goes through the CAS-guarded helpers in `lib/domain-transfer.ts`, so a re-run, two
workers, or a simultaneous customer cancel can never credit twice. `cancelTransferIn` credits the
wallet **only after the registrar confirms the cancellation**.

Constants: `TRANSFER_TERM_YEARS = 1`, `ICANN_TRANSFER_LOCK_DAYS = 60`,
`TRANSFER_TYPICAL_DAYS = "5–7 days"`, `TRANSFER_STALE_DAYS = 14`. The auth code is stored
AES-256-GCM encrypted in `Domain.transferAuthCodeEnc` and scrubbed the moment the transfer
completes or fails.

**Sandbox behaviour** (staging only): `transfersAvailable()` is true, costs are synthetic
$9–$19 by TLD hash, a name containing `locked` quotes as non-transferable, a name containing
`fail` is rejected at submit, and the status progresses `pendingOwnerApproval` → `pendingRegistry`
→ `completed` on a compressed few-minute clock. **Registration and renewal are NOT sandboxed** —
they call the real client, which throws when unconfigured.

**How an admin diagnoses it.** `/admin/domains` for the fleet. The audit log is the reconciliation
tool: `domain.register.needs_review`, `domain.register.recovered`, `domain.renew.uncharged`,
`domain.transfer_in.uncharged`. `Domain.error` carries the last registrar message.

## Cloudflare integration

**What it does.** Lets a customer connect their Cloudflare account once, after which every DNS
surface in the platform can publish records for them without a token paste.

**The flow.**

```
   Customer clicks "Connect Cloudflare" (from Settings, Email DNS,
   the Websites panel, or the post-migration cutover panel)
        │
        ▼
   GET /api/integrations/cloudflare/start
        │  requireUser; rate limit 10/60s
        │  parseIntent(...)  ← settings | email{id} | website{id} | migration{id,host?}
        │  safeNext(...)     ← forces a relative /dashboard… path, no open redirect
        │  mint state (24B) + PKCE verifier (32B)
        │  set httpOnly cookie `nx_cf_oauth` = {state, verifier, next, intent, uid}
        │      sameSite lax · path /api/integrations/cloudflare · maxAge 600
        │  302 → https://dash.cloudflare.com/oauth2/auth
        ▼
   Customer consents at Cloudflare
        ▼
   GET /api/integrations/cloudflare/callback
        │  requireUser; read + parse the cookie
        │  CSRF: `state` MUST equal the cookie's                    ← gate 1
        │  stash.uid MUST equal the current user                    ← gate 2
        │  cfExchangeCode({ code, codeVerifier })
        │  store packCreds(...) into User.cloudflareTokenEnc
        │  audit cloudflare.connect
        │  runConnectIntent(...)   ← calls the SAME ownership-checked action
        │                            the button would have called
        │  redirect to `next` with ?cf= / ?cfdns= / ?cfmsg= result flags
        │  the cookie is cleared on EVERY exit path
        ▼
   CloudflareResultBanner renders the outcome
```

Authorization Code + PKCE (S256) as a **confidential** client. Endpoints
`https://dash.cloudflare.com/oauth2/{auth,token,revoke}`, all env-overridable. Token-endpoint auth
defaults to HTTP Basic, switchable with `CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_TOKEN_AUTH=post`.

**GAP — the scope names are not confirmed.** `lib/cloudflare-oauth.ts:27-42` and `:159-165` record
that the exact Cloudflare resource-scope names could not be confirmed from public docs, and that
probing the live endpoint returned `invalid_scope` for every value tried. The code therefore sends
`scope` **only** when an operator explicitly sets `CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_SCOPES`. Production sets it to
`dns.read dns.write zone.read`. Do not present this list as verified — it is the operator's guess,
and if the integration starts failing with `invalid_scope`, that variable is the first thing to
change.

**Token storage — no schema change.** `User.cloudflareTokenEnc` holds **either** an encrypted JSON
credential blob `{accessToken, refreshToken, expiresAt, scope}` **or**, for anyone who connected
before OAuth existed, a bare encrypted API token. `readStoredCloudflare` sniffs the shape by the
leading `{`. `resolveCloudflareToken` is the single accessor: it refreshes an access token within
90 seconds of expiry, re-encrypts the merged credentials, and **keeps the old refresh token when
Cloudflare omits a rotated one**. A failed persist is survivable — the request still uses the new
token. No refresh token means a friendly "reconnect Cloudflare" message instead of a throw.

**The connect-intent mechanism** is the reason the integration feels instant. The cookie carries a
validated intent; after consent, `runConnectIntent` (`lib/cloudflare-intent-run.ts:27`) calls the
same ownership-checked, rate-limited server action the customer's button would have called. **A
connect can therefore never do more than the customer could do by hand.** `safeNext` rejects
absolute, protocol-relative, backslash and newline paths, so there is no open redirect.

**Where records are actually written.**

| Surface | Writer |
| --- | --- |
| Mail records (MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, ownership verify) | `autoCreateEmailDns` → `cfUpsertRecords` |
| Website hostname, migration cutover | `pointHostnameToIp` → `cfUpsertRecords` |

`cfUpsertRecords` (`lib/cloudflare-dns.ts:174`) queries by type and name, then PUTs the same-kind
match or POSTs a new one, with `ttl: 1` (automatic). `sameKind` (`:149`) decides what counts as a
match: an **A record always overwrites** (so a repoint cannot round-robin between the old and new
server); an **MX** matches by mail host; a **TXT** matches by its leading tag
(`nxeon-verify=`, `v=spf1`, `v=dkim1`, `v=dmarc1`) so unrelated apex TXT records are never
clobbered. Zone resolution walks hostname candidates most-specific-first, capped at 4.

**A records are always written `proxied: false`.** That is load-bearing, not a default: the name
must resolve to the customer's own server so Let's Encrypt's HTTP-01 challenge reaches certbot on
that box. Behind Cloudflare's proxy the challenge is answered at the edge and one-click SSL fails.

**Paste-a-token fallback** is kept behind an "Advanced" disclosure and is used automatically when
`CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` / `_SECRET` are unset (`cloudflareOauthConfigured()` hides the
button). `saveCloudflareToken` verifies the token with Cloudflare before storing it.

**In sandbox nothing touches Cloudflare**: `/start` stores a synthetic credential blob and runs the
intent inline, and every record write returns a clearly-labelled synthetic success.

**Setup checklist.** Register the redirect URL `<APP_URL>/api/integrations/cloudflare/callback` on
the Cloudflare OAuth client (Manage Account → OAuth clients), grant type `authorization_code`,
response type `code`.

## Nxeon Mail: mailboxes and webmail

**What it does.** A full webmail client inside the portal, talking IMAP and SMTP to the
self-hosted Mailcow instance on the `nxeon-mail` VM.

**The infrastructure.** A dedicated Debian 12 VM, vmid 8000, private `10.20.0.10`, running Mailcow
(Postfix, Dovecot, Rspamd, SOGo — about 18 containers). Mail ports 25/465/587/993/995/143/4190 are
DNAT'd from the host's main IP to the VM through a dedicated `NXEON_MAIL` iptables chain, made
persistent by `nxeon-mail-nat.service` (a oneshot with `RemainAfterExit=yes` — "inactive (dead)"
is its normal state after a successful run, not a fault). The webmail and admin UI are
reverse-proxied at `mail.nxeon.cloud`. DNS carries `mail` A, MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC records, and
the PTR points at `mail.nxeon.cloud`. Deliverability to Gmail is verified with SPF, DKIM and DMARC
passing. The platform's own transactional mailer points at this instance.

**Connection facts.**

| Fact | Value | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IMAP | `MAIL_IMAP_HOST` default `10.20.0.10`, port 993, TLS | `lib/mail/types.ts:8`, `lib/mail/imap.ts:125` |
| SMTP | default `10.20.0.10`, port 587; `secure` only on 465, else `requireTLS` | `lib/mail/types.ts:10`, `lib/actions-mail.ts:444` |
| TLS servername | `MAIL_TLS_SERVERNAME` default `mail.nxeon.cloud` | `lib/mail/imap.ts:68` |
| Certificate validation | `rejectUnauthorized: false` on both paths | `lib/mail/imap.ts:132`, `lib/actions-mail.ts:449` |

Certificate validation is relaxed **because the app dials the mail server by internal IP** while
the certificate is issued for the public hostname. The SNI servername is still set. This is a
deliberate trade-off on a private bridge, not an oversight — but it is worth revisiting.

**Keyboard map** (`components/customer/mail/MailClient.tsx:510`): `j`/`k` move, `Enter` or `o`
open, `r` reply, `a` reply all, `f` forward, `e` archive, `#` delete, `s` star, `c` compose, `/`
focus search, `?` help, `Esc` close.

**Ownership.** `resolveMailbox` (`lib/mail/imap.ts:90`) is the single entry point and never returns
a mailbox the caller does not own: `requireUser` → the user's mailboxes via
`subscription.userId` → default to the first, else a case-insensitive match, else "You do not have
access to that mailbox." Credentials are decrypted per request with `lib/crypto-box.ts`
(AES-256-GCM, key scrypt-derived from `AUTH_SECRET`). A mailbox with no stored password gives
"Please reset your mailbox password first to enable webmail access."

**Sending** — `sendMessage` (`lib/actions-mail.ts:382`):

1. `resolveMailbox`.
2. Rate limits: **5 sends per 60 s** burst and **60 per hour**, per user.
3. Recipient parsing tolerates `Name <addr>`; errors name the bad recipients.
4. Attachments: max 10, max 20 MB decoded total; base64 validated by regex and length; filenames
   stripped of control characters, quotes, backslashes and slashes, capped at 200.
5. Threading: with `inReplyToUid` and `replyFolder`, the original's envelope is fetched to set
   `In-Reply-To` and `References`, and the original is flagged `\Answered`. A failure sends without
   threading headers rather than failing the send.
6. The message is compiled **once** through a nodemailer `streamTransport`, so the exact bytes that
   are sent are the bytes appended to Sent.
7. SMTP submission authenticates as the mailbox itself.
8. The Sent copy is appended `\Seen`, best effort.

**Rate limits across the mail subsystem:** send burst 5/60s, send 60/hour, flag 240/60s, move
120/60s, delete 120/60s, settings 30/60s, alias 20/60s, signature-image upload 15/60s. The limiter
(`lib/rate-limit.ts`) is a **sliding window in a module-level Map** — in-memory, per-process, not
durable, and not coordinated across instances. It resets on every deploy.

**Rendering safety.** `safeHtml` (`lib/mail/render.ts:25`) strips script, style, iframe, object,
embed, noscript, template, frameset, frame and applet **with their content**, looping until stable;
strips standalone `link`, `meta`, `base` and `form`; removes every `on*=` handler in all three
quoting styles; and rewrites `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `data:`, `blob:` and `file:` in `href`,
`src`, `xlink:href`, `action`, `formaction`, `background`, `poster`, `data` and `srcset` to `#`,
with entity and whitespace de-obfuscation first. The result is then rendered inside
`<iframe sandbox="" srcDoc=…>` — **no `allow-scripts`, no `allow-same-origin`**.

**Attachment download** — `GET /api/mail/attachment` streams with
`Content-Disposition: attachment`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and
`Cache-Control: private, no-store`. Auth is `resolveMailbox`; unauthenticated is 401, any other
failure is 403, IMAP errors are 502.

**Failure modes the customer sees.** No mailbox or IMAP down at page load gives a full-page "No
mailbox connected" empty state with a button to `/dashboard/email`. List, open and refresh failures
raise toasts. **Mutations are optimistic**: archive, delete and move remove the row immediately and
then toast on failure — **the row does not come back**, so a failed archive looks like a lost
message until the next refresh. Send failures surface the raw SMTP error, truncated to 300
characters.

**GAP — BCC is unreachable from the UI.** `SendPayload.bcc` exists and the server parses and sends
it, but the Composer renders only To and Cc.

**GAP — `displayName`, `replyTo` and `organization` are never used when sending.** `sendMessage`
sets `from: <bare address>` and no `Reply-To` header. Those fields only seed signature templates.

**GAP — no drafts.** The Drafts folder is listed but read-only; there is no save or autosave.

**GAP — Starred and Snoozed are not what they look like.** "Snoozed" always resolves to null and
therefore always renders empty. "Starred" client-filters flagged messages out of **the current
INBOX page only** — it is not a server-side search, so a starred message on page 3 does not appear.
"Filters" is disabled with a "coming soon" label.

**GAP — the Connection panel shows a different host than the app dials.** The panel hardcodes
`mail.nxeon.cloud` (correct for the customer's own IMAP client) while the server dials
`10.20.0.10`. Both are right for their audience; do not "fix" one to match the other.

## Mailbox settings: what is real and what is stored

`components/customer/mail/MailSettings.tsx` is an eight-section modal opened from the FolderRail,
backed by `lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts`. Every action resolves through `resolveMailbox`, so
ownership is enforced once, in one place. **Half of these sections are deliberately store-only, and
the UI says so — do not let a support conversation imply otherwise.**

| Section | Action | Real? | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Signature (rich HTML) | `saveMailboxSettings` `:136` | **REAL** | Sanitised server-side with `safeHtml`, capped at 20000 chars, applied by the Composer |
| Identity (display name, reply-to, organization) | `saveMailboxSettings` `:136` | **STORE-ONLY** | Written to `Mailbox` but never read at send time |
| Auto-reply / vacation | `saveAutoReply` `:250` | **STORE-ONLY, by design** | "Mailcow's REST API exposes no reliable vacation endpoint. We do NOT pretend the mail server sends them." (`:241`) |
| Forwarding | `saveForwarding` `:213` | **STORE-ONLY, by design** | "STORE-ONLY and honestly labelled as such in the UI" (`:203`) |
| Aliases | `listAliases` `:295`, `addAlias` `:318`, `removeAlias` `:348` | **REAL** | Mailcow API; domain ownership re-checked against the user's `EmailSubscription.domainName` set on every call |
| Storage | read-only | **REAL (read)** | Live IMAP QUOTA, falling back to the plan quota with an honest note |
| Connection details | static | display only | Copyable IMAP/SMTP settings |
| Password | `resetPassword` `:376` | **REAL** | Owner-checked, rate-limited, **Mailcow first** — the new value is persisted only after the mail server accepts it |

**The signature editor** is a hand-rolled `contentEditable` with bold, italic, underline, font
family and size, colour, bullet and numbered lists, link, image (upload from the computer, URL as
fallback), horizontal rule, clear-format, an image-size bar (Small 150 / Medium 320 / Large 600 /
Full width, plus a 40–1000 px slider), three starter templates, a live preview, an "include on
replies and forwards" toggle and a Below/Above placement segment. Everything is sanitised with
`safeHtml` three times: in the client preview, on the server at save, and in the Composer at send.

**Signature images** live in Postgres (`SignatureImage`), not on disk, because the web process runs
non-root and can only write `.next`. `POST /api/mail/signature-image` validates by magic bytes,
rejects SVG, caps at 5 MB and 20 images per user (pruning the oldest), and returns an **absolute
https URL** so the image renders in external inboxes where there is no session.

**Signature assembly is client-side** (`Composer.tsx:169`): `signatureHtml` preferred, else the
plain text wrapped in `-- <br>`; the text part gets `\n\n-- \n<sig>`. Placement `above` gives
user text, signature, quote; `below` (the default) gives user text, quote, signature.

**Ordering** — `orderEmailHosting` (`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:231`): domain normalised and

be active, one non-CANCELLED subscription per domain, promo applies to the first term only, balance
checked. One transaction does debit, `WalletTransaction`, and the `EmailSubscription` with
`expiresAt = now + plan.termMonths`. External domains get `verified: false` and a random
`verifyToken`.

**The five DNS records** — `getEmailDnsRecords` (`:326`), constants at `:34`:

| Type | Host | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TXT | `_nxeon-verify.<domain>` | `nxeon-verify=<verifyToken>` |
| MX | `<domain>` | `mail.nxeon.cloud`, priority 10 |
| TXT | `<domain>` | `v=spf1 include:nxeon.cloud ~all` |
| TXT | `dkim._domainkey.<domain>` | from Mailcow, cached into `EmailSubscription.dkimRecord` |
| TXT | `_dmarc.<domain>` | `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@nxeon.cloud` |

An empty DKIM value shows "DKIM key is being generated on the mail server — refresh this page
shortly."

**Verification** — `verifyEmailDomain` (`:418`). The primary signal is a TXT lookup on
`_nxeon-verify.<domain>` whose joined chunks **exactly equal** `nxeon-verify=<token>`. MX is
corroboration only and never substitutes. Rate limit 6 per 60 s.

**Provisioning is synchronous, not a job.** `provisionMailboxOnMailcow` (`:81`) runs inside the
server action: ensure the domain exists in Mailcow, generate a password, create the mailbox, store
`passwordEnc` and set `ACTIVE`. Any throw sets `FAILED` and logs — it never throws out. **There is
no `JobType` for email anywhere in the enum.**

**Renewal and suspension.** `worker/product-renewals.ts` warns at T−3 days, charges at T+0 with a
compare-and-swap on `expiresAt` and a PAID invoice in the same transaction, and at the end of grace
sets `EmailSubscription.status = SUSPENDED` — **mailboxes are never deleted**.

**GAP — every mailbox renders as "Provisioning".** `components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx:345`
hardcodes an amber "Provisioning" badge, and the client row type never carries the status
(`MailboxRow` is only `{id, address, createdAt}`). An ACTIVE mailbox and a FAILED one look
identical to the customer. This is a small fix with a large support-cost impact.

**GAP — suspend/resume and retry are unreachable.** `setMailboxSuspended` and
`retryMailboxProvision` are exported and called from no UI. A `FAILED` mailbox has no
customer-facing recovery path; staff must call the action or fix it in Mailcow directly.

**How an admin diagnoses it.** `/admin/mail` is the deliverability dashboard (Postfix and Rspamd
stats). `/admin/email-plans` manages the tiers. On the mail VM, the Mailcow admin UI at
`mail.nxeon.cloud` is authoritative for whether a mailbox actually exists. See "Runbook: checking
mail deliverability".

  dashboard has no active-org switcher yet" — with the exact patch to apply.

The scope is stated in the source too (`lib/actions-teams.ts:16`): shared billing and members
inheriting access to shared servers are **deliberately out of scope**, and nothing in Teams changes
server ownership. So today: a member gains no access to the owner's servers, wallet or invoices,
and area grants are stored but never checked. **Do not sell Teams as access control.**

## Support tickets and live chat

**Tickets.** Models `Ticket` and `TicketMessage`; statuses `OPEN`, `ANSWERED`, `CUSTOMER_REPLY`,
`CLOSED`; priorities `LOW`, `NORMAL`, `HIGH`, `URGENT`.

```
  /dashboard/support                        /admin/support   (requireArea "support")
┌──────────────────────────────────┐      ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Subject   Status  Pri  Msgs  Upd │      │ Subject  Customer  Pri  Status  Msgs │
│ Can't SSH  OPEN   HIGH   3  2h   │      │ Can't SSH  bob@…    HIGH  OPEN    3  │
│ [ New ticket ]                   │      └──────────────────────────────────────┘
└──────────────────────────────────┘
  /dashboard/support/[id]
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ┌─ staff ────────────────┐                                   │
│  │ Have you tried port…   │                                   │
│  └────────────────────────┘   ┌────────────── customer ─────┐ │
│                               │ Yes, same result.           │ │
│                               └─────────────────────────────┘ │
│  [ Reply…                                          ] [ Send ] │
│    (hidden when the ticket is CLOSED)                         │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

`createTicket` (`lib/actions-support.ts:9`) validates subject 3–150 and body 5–10000, creates the
ticket with its first message, and **notifies every ADMIN** with a link to `/admin/support/<id>`.
`replyTicket` (`:43`) computes `isStaff` as "ADMIN and not the ticket owner", refuses anyone who is
neither owner nor admin, and in one transaction creates the message and flips the status to
`ANSWERED` (staff) or `CUSTOMER_REPLY` (customer), then notifies the counterpart.
`setTicketPriority` is ADMIN-only.

**GAP — no rate limiting on ticket creation or replies.** `lib/actions-support.ts` does not import
`checkRateLimit`. A logged-in account can create tickets in a loop, and each one notifies every
admin.

**Live chat.** A first-party widget, not a third-party script. `components/ChatWidget.tsx` polls
every 4 seconds, stores an anonymous `visitorId` in `localStorage`, and supports paste-to-attach
and image upload.

Every public endpoint is scoped strictly by the client-supplied `visitorId`:

| Endpoint | Rate limit | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/chat` | 30/60 s per IP | Continues the visitor's OPEN conversation or creates one; sets `unreadForAgent` |
| `GET /api/chat?visitorId=` | — | Returns the OPEN conversation; **reading clears `unreadForUser`** |
| `GET /api/chat/[id]?visitorId=` | — | `findFirst({ id, visitorId })` — guessing an id returns nothing |
| `POST /api/chat/upload` | 15/60 s per IP | 5 MB cap before buffering; bytes signature-validated; SVG rejected |
| `GET /api/chat/attachment/[id]` | — | Authorised for staff, the matching `visitorId`, or the linked `userId`; served with the real stored MIME plus `nosniff` and a `default-src 'none'` CSP |

Staff side (`lib/actions-chat.ts`) is entirely gated on `requireArea("support")`. Replying sets
`status: OPEN`, `unreadForUser: true`, `unreadForAgent: false`, assigns the conversation to the
replying staff member, and notifies the linked customer. Admin inbox at `/admin/chat` with Open,
Unread and Total stat cards.

Attachment bytes live in Postgres (`ChatAttachment`), not on disk, for the same reason as signature
images: the non-root web process cannot write to the filesystem.

## Notifications

**What it does.** The in-app bell. One model, `Notification { title, body?, href?, readAt?, userId }`,
written from **21 files across 37 call sites** — five in the app layer
(`actions-domains`, `actions-feedback`, `actions-growth`, `actions-support`, `stripe`) and sixteen
in the worker.

```
┌─ portal header ──────────────────────────────┐
│  …                              🔔 [3]   ▾   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        ▼  w-80, max-h-80 scroll
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ● Server web1 is ready                       │
│   ssh root@51.79.162.181                     │
│   25/07/2026, 14:02:11                       │
│ ● example.com renews soon — action needed    │
│   Renewal is $12.99 but your balance is …    │
│ ○ Backup completed for web1                  │
│   ─────────────────────────────────────────  │
│   "All caught up." when empty                │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Opening the panel marks everything read** (`markNotificationsRead` in a transition). Only the
most recent **15** are loaded server-side, so a busy account's bell is a recent-events view, not a
log. The customer's `/dashboard/activity` page is the fuller history.

**Worker dedupe pattern.** `notifyOnce` (`worker/product-renewals.ts:83`) looks for an existing
notification within a dedupe window whose title contains both a stable entity label (the hostname
or domain) and a marker phrase ("renews soon", "will be deleted"). `notify` itself is fully
best-effort — a notify failure must never roll back a charge.

**GAP — notification preferences are store-only.** `NotificationPrefs = {email, product, security}`
(`lib/prefs.ts:11`), all defaulting true, are written by `updateNotificationPrefs` and rendered in
Settings. A full grep for `normalizePrefs|notificationPrefs` returns six hits: the writer, the
settings page, the GDPR export, and the definition. **No `db.notification.create` call site and no
path in `lib/mailer.ts` consults them.** Turning off "product news" or "security alerts" changes
nothing.

## API tokens and the public API

**Token format.** `nxe_<prefix>_<secret>` where `prefix` is 8 hex characters (public, stored for
display) and `secret` is 24 random bytes base64url. Only the **sha256 hex** of the whole token is
stored, in the unique column `ApiToken.tokenHash`. The plaintext is returned exactly once at
creation.

```
┌─ Settings → API tokens ───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Name [ ci-deploy        ]   Expires in [ never ▾ ] days              │
│  Scopes  [x] read   [ ] write                     [ Create token ]    │
│  ┌─ Save this token — it is shown once ─────────────────────────┐     │
│  │  nxe_a1b2c3d4_9Xk…                                  [ copy ] │     │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│  Name        Prefix      Scopes   Last used     Expires   Actions     │
│  ci-deploy   a1b2c3d4    read     2h ago        never     [ Revoke ]  │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Authentication** — `authenticateApiToken` (`lib/api-auth.ts:38`): bearer extracted
case-insensitively, must start `nxe_`, looked up by hash. 401 for missing, invalid, revoked or
expired; 403 for a missing or suspended user. `lastUsedAt` is stamped fire-and-forget so it never
blocks the request.

**Scope resolution** — `tokenHasScope` (`:79`):

- **An empty `scopes` array means FULL ACCESS.** This is an explicit backward-compatibility policy
  for tokens minted before scopes existed (`:68`). Know it before you audit anything.
- `*` or an exact match passes.
- A resource wildcard `servers:*` satisfies `servers:read`.
- A generic `read` satisfies any `*:read`.

**The entire public API is one endpoint.** `GET /api/v1/servers` requires `servers:read` and
returns `{ servers: [{id, name, status, ip}] }` for the caller's own servers.
`find app/api/v1 -type f` returns exactly one file. **A `write`-only token can call nothing.**

**GAP — no rate limit and no cap on token count.** `createApiToken` has neither. Revocation is a
soft delete (`revoked: true`); the row is retained.

**GAP — token hashing is unsalted sha256.** Adequate for a 24-byte random secret (there is nothing
to guess), but it is not a password hash and should not be described as one.

---

## Two-factor authentication and account security

**TOTP** — `lib/totp.ts`, dependency-free RFC 6238: HMAC-SHA1, 6 digits, 30-second step, a
20-byte (160-bit) base32 secret. Verification uses a **±1 step window** with `timingSafeEqual` per
step and rejects anything that is not exactly six digits. Issuer in the otpauth URL is `Nxeon`.
Covered by tests against the RFC 6238 vectors.

**Enrolment.**

```
   beginTotpEnrollment()                       lib/actions-2fa.ts:75
     · REFUSES while impersonating (realUser().id !== user.id)
     · REFUSES to overwrite an already-active secret
       ← an earlier bug here silently disabled working 2FA
     · stores totpSecretEnc (AES-256-GCM), nulls any legacy plaintext
        ▼
   confirmTotpEnrollment(code)                            :101
     · verify → totpEnabled = true
     · generate 10 backup codes, store ONLY their hashes
     · audit user.2fa_enabled
        ▼
   regenerateBackupCodes(code)                            :122   requires a valid TOTP code
   disableTotp(...)                                       :138   accepts a TOTP code
                                                                 OR a backup code
                                                                 OR the account password
```

Backup codes are `xxxxx-xxxxx` from 5 random bytes, stored as the sha256 of the lower-cased trimmed
code, **single-use** (consumed by index removal at verification time, audited as
`user.2fa_backup_code_used`). `totpSecretOf` prefers the encrypted column and falls back to the
legacy plaintext one so already-enrolled users keep working.

**Login** — `login` (`lib/actions.ts:141`):

1. Zod credentials.
2. Rate limit keyed `login:<email>:<ip>` over a **15-minute** window; the max is the
   `login_ratelimit_max` setting, **default 10**. (`lib/rate-limit.ts:53` also exposes a
   `loginRateLimit` preset of 5 per 15 minutes; the login path does **not** use it.)
3. `bcrypt.compare`, with a deliberately generic "Invalid email or password." for both unknown
   user and bad password.
4. Suspended accounts get "This account is suspended."
5. With `totpEnabled`, a missing or bad code returns `{ needs2fa: true }`, which drives the
   second-step UI.
6. On success: reset the rate limit, audit `user.login`, create the session, redirect ADMIN to
   `/admin` and everyone else to `/dashboard`.

**Sessions.** A `jose` HS256 JWT signed with `AUTH_SECRET` carrying `{sub, sv}`, where `sv` is the
account's `sessionVersion` at issue time. Lifetime comes from the `session_length_days` setting
(default 30) and is applied to both the JWT expiry and the cookie `maxAge`.

Two cookies: the httpOnly session, and a **non-httpOnly, identity-free `nxeon_authed=1`** flag so
the statically-rendered marketing header can show "Dashboard" without a server round trip. Both are
cleared together.

**Revocation works through `sessionVersion`.** `realUser()` rejects a token whose `sv` does not
match the user's current `sessionVersion`; a missing `sv` counts as 0, so accounts that never
bumped stay signed in. It is bumped on password change and on password reset — and in the
password-change path the current session is immediately re-issued so the person changing their
password is not logged out.

**Impersonation.** A separate `<cookie>_imp` JWT with a **2-hour** expiry whose `adminId` must match
the real admin. `currentUser()` returns the target; `realUser()` returns the admin. Admin pages
refuse to render while impersonating. `assertNotImpersonating()` guards every spend path — top-up,
deploy, transfer submit, transfer cancel — so an admin can never move a customer's money on their
behalf.

**Staff 2FA can be forced.** With the `enforce_staff_2fa` setting on, `app/admin/layout.tsx:95`
blocks any staff member without `totpEnabled`.

**Understand the rate limiter's limits.** `lib/rate-limit.ts` is a sliding window over a
module-level `Map`, HMR-persisted in development, swept opportunistically at most once a minute.
It is **in-memory and per-process**: it does not survive a restart and does not coordinate across
instances. nginx's own auth rate-limit on the login and register routes is the durable layer.

---

## Referrals, coupons, gift codes and the affiliate program

**Referrals.** Every user gets a unique `referralCode`. The referred user's first paid action — a
top-up or an order — rewards both sides once via `maybeRewardReferral`
(`lib/actions-growth.ts:258`), wired into both the demo and Stripe credit paths.
`REFERRAL_REWARD_CENTS` defaults to $5. `User.referralRewardedAt` makes it once-only.

**Signup credit.** `SIGNUP_FREE_CREDIT_CENTS` / the `signup_free_credit_cents` setting, applied by
`grantSignupCredit` (`:230`). Default 0 — deliberately off, because there is no email verification
yet and free credit without verification is an invitation to abuse.

**Coupons.** `Coupon` with `kind` in `PERCENT`, `FIXED_CENTS`, `CREDIT_CENTS`; `scope` in `ANY`,
`TOPUP`, `ORDER`; plus `firstTimeOnly`, `minAmountCents`, `maxRedemptions`, `timesRedeemed`,
`expiresAt`, `active`. `CouponRedemption` is unique on `(couponId, userId)`, so one redemption per
user per coupon is enforced by the database, not by application logic. Applied at top-up by
`applyCouponToTopup` (`:63`). Admin CRUD at `/admin/coupons`.

**Gift codes.** `GiftCode` with `amountCents` and a nullable `redeemedById` / `redeemedAt`. Created
in batches by `adminCreateGiftCodes` (`lib/actions-gift.ts:47`), redeemed by `redeemGiftCode`
(`:106`). Admin surface `/admin/gift-codes`.

**Affiliate.** `AffiliatePayout` with `status` in `PENDING`, `APPROVED`, `PAID`, `DECLINED`.
Earnings are computed from the referral ledger; the customer dashboard is `/dashboard/affiliate`
with a $25 minimum payout request (`requestAffiliatePayout`, `lib/actions-affiliate.ts:40`), and
admin management is `/admin/affiliate` (`adminUpdatePayout`, `:128`).

**Feature flag.** `coupons_enabled` gates the coupon field.

---

## Bandwidth metering and abuse detection

**GAP — bandwidth metering does not exist.** This is the most important thing on this page.

The fields are all there: `Server.bwInBytes`, `bwOutBytes`, `bwWindowStart`, `abuseBwMark`,
`abuseBwMarkAt`, and the allowance on `Plan.bandwidthTB`. An exhaustive grep for
`bwInBytes|bwOutBytes|bwWindowStart|abuseBwMark` across the whole repo returns exactly five sites:

| Site | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `prisma/schema.prisma:314-318` | Declaration |
| `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx:56` | Read |
| `worker/abuse.ts:8` | A comment referring to "the metering sweep" |
| `worker/abuse.ts:25`, `:35` | Read |
| `worker/abuse.ts:32` | Write — but it only copies `bwOutBytes` into `abuseBwMark` |

**`bwInBytes` and `bwOutBytes` are never incremented anywhere.** There is no metering sweep; the
comment refers to code that does not exist. Proxmox `netin`/`netout` are read for the live charts
on the server and node metric panels and are never persisted.

**Three consequences, all verified:**

1. **Every customer's bandwidth meter reads 0 B and 0%** on `/dashboard/billing`, for every server.
   The amber-over-80% and red-over-100% thresholds can never fire.
2. **There is no bandwidth enforcement or overage billing of any kind.** `Plan.bandwidthTB` is
   displayed on the pricing grid, the deploy wizard and both server detail pages, and is used
   nowhere else. Nothing throttles, suspends or charges for exceeding it. **The advertised TB
   allowance is currently unmetered and unenforced — treat it as a marketing figure, not a limit.**
3. **The outbound-abuse detector is inert.** `abuseSweep` (`worker/abuse.ts:16`) runs every 10
   minutes, computes `deltaBytes = bwOutBytes − abuseBwMark`, and skips when the delta is not
   positive. Since `bwOutBytes` is permanently 0, the delta is always 0 and every server is skipped
   on every pass. **No `BANDWIDTH_SPIKE` `AbuseAlert` can ever be raised**, so `abuse_outbound_mbps`
   (default 200) and `abuse_autosuspend` (default false) are dead settings and `/admin/abuse` will
   stay empty for this alert kind.

**What monitoring does work.** `monitorSweep` (`worker/monitor.ts:124`) alerts admins on disk above
85%, worker-down, stuck jobs and stale backups. `sampleServerDisks` (`:68`) samples in-guest disk
usage from the QEMU guest agent into `ServerDiskSample` on a rolling ~35-day window, which is what
feeds the customer's disk-usage-over-time chart (Proxmox RRD reports `disk=0` for QEMU VMs, so it
cannot feed that chart).

**What an admin can actually see today.** Instantaneous per-VM throughput from the Proxmox RRD, on
`/dashboard/servers/[id]`, `/admin/servers/[id]` and `/admin/nodes/[id]`. There is no cumulative
figure anywhere in the database. For a real answer, query Proxmox or the host directly.

---

## Dedicated IPv4 addresses

**What it does.** Gives a VM its own public IPv4 from the OVH failover pool instead of sharing one
behind NAT. Since the plan-price consolidation, `dedicated_ip_price_cents` defaults to `0` and a
dedicated IP is included in every plan, which is why "dedicated IP included" is honest.

**The pool.** `lib/dedicated-ip.ts` syncs OVH failover IPs into the `DedicatedIp` table; the worker
refreshes it every 5 minutes. On allocation it claims a `FREE` row, **creates the OVH Virtual MAC**
(an asynchronous OVH task, so the code polls until it appears), and attaches the VM to `vmbr0` with
that MAC and `ip=<addr>/32,gw=51.79.162.254`.

**The lifecycle that matters.**

```
   PROVISION   → allocate (idempotent: a retry returns the server's already-ASSIGNED IP
                 rather than claiming a second pool address)
   SUSPEND     → RELEASE back to the pool + null Server.ipAddress
                 (ipAddress is UNIQUE — leaving it set makes the next claimant fail P2002)
   UNSUSPEND   → re-allocate, or fall back to shared NAT with a fresh private IP + SSH port
   DELETE      → release the IP and delete the billable OVH Virtual MAC
   PROVISION fails terminally → release the IP and clear Server.ipAddress
```

**Billing reads the relation, not the intent.** `worker/billing.ts:112` bills the IP surcharge only
when a `DedicatedIp` row is actually attached, never off `Server.wantsDedicatedIp` — so a server
that fell back to NAT because the pool was empty is not charged forever for an address it never
received.

**Low-pool alert.** With `dedicated_ip_autoreplenish` on, the worker notifies admins when the free
count drops below `dedicated_ip_replenish_threshold` (default 2), deduped to once per 6 hours.
**Auto-ordering IPs is deliberately not built** — it spends real money at OVH and stays a manual
admin action.

**How an admin diagnoses it.** `/admin/ips` shows the pool with cost, revenue and margin per
address. A server on NAT that should have a public IP is almost always an empty pool at provision
time; check `SELECT status, count(*) FROM "DedicatedIp" GROUP BY status;`.

---

## Build with AI and Claude Code

**What it does.** Two related things that used to be confusingly presented as one.

**1. Claude Code is pre-installed on every VPS.** `buildCloudInit` (`worker/index.ts:92`) installs
Node 20, `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` and git on first boot — in the background, so "ready" is not
delayed — writes `/root/START-WITH-CLAUDE.md`, and adds a `/etc/profile.d` login banner pointing at
the portal hub. On by default; opt out with `addons.claudeCode: false`.

The customer authenticates as **themselves**, with their own Claude subscription or their own
Anthropic API key. Zero token cost to the platform, no account sharing. This is a deliberate policy
position: the operator's personal Claude.ai subscription is never tucked behind customers, because
account sharing violates Anthropic's terms and would expose the credential on untrusted VMs. The
only legitimate paths are the customer's own subscription or key (this feature), or a platform API
key with metering (not built).

**2. The in-app AI build planner** at `/dashboard/build` — bring-your-own-key, plan-then-approve.
Claude proposes shell commands; the customer approves before anything runs over SSH. Guarded by a
denylist, a 20-command cap and timeouts. `ClaudeBuild` rows track
`QUEUED → PLANNING → AWAITING_APPROVAL → RUNNING → DONE|FAILED`; the worker handler is
`claudeBuild` (`worker/claude.ts:159`). Actions: `submitBuild` (`lib/actions-claude.ts:30`),
`approveBuild` (`:113`), `rejectBuild` (`:145`), `listBuilds` (`:169`).

**Navigation.** There is exactly **one** sidebar entry under Compute — "Build with AI" pointing at
`/dashboard/claude-code`. The planner route is kept (notifications from `worker/claude.ts` link to
it) but de-navved, and its header reads "AI build planner". The BYOK key lives in Settings, at
`/dashboard/settings#anthropic-key`, encrypted into `User.anthropicKeyEnc` with AES-256-GCM.

**The hub** (`/dashboard/claude-code`) is content, not machinery: a three-step quick start with a
mock terminal auto-filled with the user's real `ssh` command; a setup walkthrough tabbed
subscription-versus-API-key; a searchable library of 36 copy-paste prompt templates with a
fill-in-the-blank editor; and an accordion of how-to guides. All of it is a pure data module,
`lib/ai-build.ts`, with no IO, so it is safe to import anywhere.

---

## The admin portal

Forty-six pages, grouped into six sidebar sections. `app/admin/layout.tsx` renders one visible
`NavSection` per group with every item listed beneath its header, filtered by role, with empty
groups dropped and per-route badge counts on individual rows.

| Group | Pages |
| --- | --- |
| Insights | `/admin` (overview), `analytics`, `visitors` |
| Customers | `users` (+`[id]` customer-360), `orgs`, `support` (+`[id]`), `chat`, `feedback` |
| Fleet | `servers` (+`[id]`), `nodes` (+`new`, +`[id]`), `ips`, `provisioning`, `jobs`, `monitoring`, `abuse`, `infrastructure` |
| Revenue | `billing`, `invoices` (+`[id]`), `subscriptions`, `plans`, `products`, `coupons`, `gift-codes`, `game-plans`, `email-plans`, `affiliate` |
| Platform | `settings`, `staff`, `domains`, `grant`, `games`, `email-templates`, `mail`, `newsletter`, `blog`, `testimonials`, `docs`, `improvements`, `automation` |
| System | `audit`, `logs` |

**The pages you will actually use.**

- **`/admin/provisioning`** — queued, running and failed-in-24h counts plus the last 30 failures.
  First stop for "a deploy is stuck".
- **`/admin/jobs`** — the last 100 jobs with `attempts` and the truncated `error`.
- **`/admin/users/[id]`** — the customer-360: servers, wallet ledger, invoices, tickets, audit
  trail, one-click impersonation, credit and suspend.
- **`/admin/billing`** — the wallet ledger with search, 30-day and lifetime charge sums, and total
  customer liability.
- **`/admin/logs`** — audit trail, activity feed, and the email log with a per-message rendered
  preview.
- **`/admin/audit`** — the `AuditLog` table. Every money movement and every destructive action
  writes here. It is the reconciliation tool of last resort.
- **`/admin/settings`** — a ten-tab, `Setting`-backed console: branding, billing, domains,
  dedicated IP, provisioning, growth, email and templates, security, feature flags, staff and
  roles.
- **`/admin/email-templates`** — a live sandboxed-iframe preview of all 31 transactional templates,
  grouped Account / Billing / Servers / Domains and SSL / Email / Support, with realistic sample
  data.
- **`/admin/improvements`** — the board written by the nightly scanner
  (`nxeon-nightly-scan.timer` → `scripts/nightly-scan.ts`).
- **`/admin/docs`** — this document.

**Impersonation** sets a signed 2-hour cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target and `realUser()`
the actual admin, with a banner and an exit control in the shell. **Admin pages refuse to render
while impersonating**, and every spend path calls `assertNotImpersonating()`.

**The portal shell** (`components/portal/Shell.tsx`) is shared by both portals: sidebar, topbar,
notifications bell, and a ⌘K command palette backed by `/api/search`. The sidebar has a
desktop-only collapse toggle that shrinks the rail to a ~76 px icon strip, persisted in
`localStorage["nxeon.portal.railCollapsed"]`; all collapse styles are gated to the `lg:`
breakpoint, so mobile always uses the full hamburger drawer.

---

## RBAC: staff roles and areas

**Two different `requireArea` functions exist.** `lib/rbac.ts:99` governs the **admin portal** and
is live. `lib/team-guard.ts:16` governs **customer organisation areas** and is imported by nothing.
Do not conflate them.

**The admin model** — `lib/rbac.ts`. Seven areas, each mapped to the roles allowed in it. ADMIN is
implicitly allowed everywhere (`canAccess`, `:34`).

| Area | SUPPORT | BILLING | ADMIN |
| --- | :--: | :--: | :--: |
| `overview` | yes | yes | yes |
| `analytics` | — | — | yes |
| `clients` | yes | — | yes |
| `support` | yes | — | yes |
| `fleet` | — | — | yes |
| `billing` | — | yes | yes |
| `platform` | — | — | yes |

**Route mapping** — `HREF_AREA` (`lib/rbac.ts:44`) maps every admin href to its governing area, and
**anything unmapped defaults to `platform`, which is ADMIN-only**. That default is the important
safety property: a new admin page added without touching `rbac.ts` is ADMIN-only until someone
deliberately opens it up.

**Three layers of enforcement.**

1. `app/admin/layout.tsx` admits any staff role and filters the navigation with `canAccessHref`.
2. Each sensitive page calls `requireArea(...)` itself, so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
3. `requireArea` redirects to `/login` when signed out, to `/dashboard` for a non-staff role, and
   to `/admin` when the staff role cannot reach that area — it never renders a partial page.

**Roles are assigned at `/admin/staff`**, ADMIN-only (`lib/actions-staff.ts`). Staff 2FA can be
forced with the `enforce_staff_2fa` setting.

#!/bin/bash
# Promote the currently deployed staging commit to production.
# Verifies staging is healthy, fast-forwards nothing (prod working tree IS the repo),
# then rebuilds + restarts production services.
set -euo pipefail

STG_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon-staging rev-parse HEAD)
PROD_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon rev-parse HEAD)

echo "==> Staging is at:    $STG_COMMIT"
echo "==> Production is at: $PROD_COMMIT"

if ! systemctl is-active -q nxeon-staging-web; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging web service is not running." >&2
  exit 1
fi
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
if [ "$CODE" != "200" ]; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging returns HTTP $CODE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$STG_COMMIT" != "$PROD_COMMIT" ]; then
  echo "Note: production tree is at a different commit than staging."
  echo "Production deploys directly from /opt/nxeon's working tree (main)."
fi

cd /opt/nxeon
echo "==> Building production"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4
=== deploy-staging ===
#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"

Idempotent / re-runnable. set -euo pipefail BACKUP_DIR="/tank/backup/db" RETENTION_DAYS="${NXEON_DB_RETENTION_DAYS:-14}" DATABASES=(nxeon nxeon_staging) TS="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)" mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR" log() { echo "[$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)] $*"; } rc=0 for db in "${DATABASES[@]}"; do # Skip cleanly if the database does not exist (e.g. staging removed). if ! sudo -u postgres psql -tAc "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='${db}'" | grep -q 1; then === verify-restore === #!/usr/bin/env bash # Restore-verification: proves the newest production dump is actually restorable. # # Restores the latest /tank/backup/db/nxeon-*.sql.gz into a scratch database, # asserts that core tables restored with rows, then drops the scratch database. # Production data is never touched. Exits non-zero on any failure so the # systemd OnFailure hook alerts admins. set -uo pipefail BACKUP_DIR="/tank/backup/db" SCRATCH="nxeon_restore_verify" LOG="/tmp/nxeon-verify-restore.log" log() { echo "[$(date -Is)] $*"; } fail() { log "FAIL: $*"; sudo -u postgres psql -qc "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ${SCRATCH};" >/dev/null 2>&1; exit 1; } LATEST="$(ls -1t "${BACKUP_DIR}"/nxeon-*.sql.gz 2>/dev/null | head -1)" [ -n "${LATEST}" ] || fail "no production dump found in ${BACKUP_DIR}" AGE_H=$(( ( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "${LATEST}") ) / 3600 )) === offsite === #!/usr/bin/env bash # Off-box backup replication. # # Copies /tank/backup/db (and optionally VM dumps) to an OFFSITE target so a # chassis/disk loss doesn't take the backups with it. Inert until configured — # set ONE of the following in /etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env: # # OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE="b2:nxeon-backups" # rclone remote (Backblaze B2, S3, OVH Object Storage…) # OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET="user@host:/backups/nxeon" # rsync over SSH (rsync.net etc.) # OFFSITE_INCLUDE_VMS=1 # optional: also replicate VM dumps (large) # # Exits non-zero on a real failure so the systemd OnFailure hook alerts admins. set -uo pipefail ENV_FILE="/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env" === diag-email === import { sendMail } from "../lib/mailer"; import { db } from "../lib/db"; async function main() { const to = process.argv[2] || "haxkodi@gmail.com"; const stamp = new Date().toISOString(); const ok = await sendMail({ to, subject: `Nxeon diagnostic test — ${stamp}`, html: `

This is an automated Nxeon deliverability + email-log diagnostic.

Sent at ${stamp}.

`, kind: "diagnostic", } as any); console.log("sendMail returned:", ok); await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 800)); const row = await db.emailLog.findFirst({ where: { toEmail: to }, orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" }, select: { id: true, toEmail: true, subject: true, status: true, error: true, createdAt: true },
